First shrink striped images to half their width and enlarge them back, giving each new pixel's sample position as well; then judge which of the original's columns survive.

brief.zh: 把输入的图缩到一半宽（高不变），交出缩小的图、每个新像素在原图里的 x，以及缩小的图再放大回原宽的样子。
brief.en: Shrink the input to half its width (height unchanged), and give the shrunk image, each new pixel's x in the original, and the shrunk image enlarged back to the original width.

hint.zh: 缩小后再放大，宽回来了：原图里的值也都回来了吗？
hint.en: Shrinking and then enlarging brings the width back: does it bring back every value of the original too?

value.zh: 量化器把每个值存成最近的一级。这一关的问题是：量化以后，原来的值还能找回来吗？先让量化器存一张图，同时交出每一格的原值可能落在的范围；再反过来，从几组输入里找出存成同一个结果的那些。
value.en: The quantiser stores each value as the nearest level. This level asks: after quantisation, can the original values be recovered? First have the quantiser store an image and give, for each cell, the range its original value may lie in; then go backwards and find, among several inputs, those stored as one same result.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和级数 L：交出量化的结果，以及每一格的原值可能在的范围，从 low 到 high（都在 [0, 1] 里）。
brief.en: Given an image and a number of levels L, give the quantised result and, for each cell, the range its original may lie in, from low to high (both within [0, 1]).

hint.zh: 相邻两级隔多远？一个值离它存成的那一级，最远能有多远？
hint.en: How far apart are two neighbouring levels? How far can a value lie from the level it is stored as?

brief.zh: 输入一张图和级数 L：交出量化的结果，以及原值减去结果的差。
brief.en: Given an image and a number of levels L, give the quantised result and the original minus the result.

value.zh: 量化器把每个值存成最近的一级。这一关的问题是：量化以后，原来的值还能找回来吗？先让量化器存一张图，同时交出每个值被改了多少；再反过来，从几组输入里找出存成同一个结果的那些。
value.en: The quantiser stores each value as the nearest level. This level asks: after quantisation, can the original values be recovered? First have the quantiser store an image and give how much each value was changed; then go backwards and find, among several inputs, those stored as one same result.

brief.zh: 把输入的图缩到一半宽（高不变），并交出每个新像素在原图里的 x。
brief.en: Shrink the input to half its width (height unchanged), and give each new pixel's x in the original.

value.zh: 最近邻缩放放大时成块。这一关换一个方向：最近邻缩小图像时，没被选中的旧像素去了哪里？先把条纹图缩到一半宽，同时交出每个新像素的采样位置，再判断原图的哪些列留在了结果里。
value.en: Nearest-neighbour enlarging makes squares. This level goes the other way: when nearest neighbour shrinks an image, what becomes of the old pixels it does not pick? First shrink striped images to half their width, giving each new pixel's sample position as well, then judge which of the original's columns survive.

why.zh: 把焦距拉长想看清楚些：每支箭都变大，两端的落到了传感器外面。
why.en: Lengthening the focal length to see better: every arrow grows, and the outer ones fall off the sensor.

value.zh: 调焦距，让三支箭的像都落在传感器上。
value.en: Set the focal length so all three arrows image on the sensor.

value.zh: 台上只有像平面的距离 f 能动。先在台上让像高达到目标，再对另外两组数不上台、先算出 f。
value.en: Only the plane distance f turns on the bench. First bring the image to the target height there, then, for two other sets of numbers, work out f without the bench.

why: Copy step: entries for the field's other terms (tasks, camera, image, libraries), each opened where it first comes in; the group retitled; the aspect-ratio example set right

ops.zh: 视觉术语
ops.en: Vision terms

body.zh: 回答「整张图主要是什么」：给整张图一个或少量类别标签（dog），不说物体在哪里，也不说有几个。讲义也叫识别。检测再给每个物体一个位置，分割把答案细化到每个像素。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: Answers what the image mainly shows: one or a few class labels for the whole image (dog), saying neither where the objects are nor how many there are. The lectures also call it recognition. Detection adds a position for each object, and segmentation refines the answer down to each pixel. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (slide 7).

body.zh: 框住一个物体的矩形，用左上角和右下角两个像素坐标写出，例如 (4, 10)–(20, 26)。检测给每个物体一个类别和一个边界框；只有框、没有类别，说了在哪里，没说是什么。框只给出大致的范围，哪些像素属于物体要由分割回答。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: The rectangle around an object, written as two pixel coordinates, its top-left and bottom-right corners, such as (4, 10)–(20, 26). Detection gives each object a class and a bounding box; a box without a class says where but not what. A box gives only the rough extent: which pixels belong to the object is for segmentation to answer. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (slide 7).

body.zh: 给每个像素标出它属于哪一类（道路、天空、人）。它只说「哪一类」，不说「哪一个」：同一类的几个物体挨在一起时连成一片，从图上数不出个数。要分开同类的各个物体，用实例分割。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: Labels each pixel with the class it belongs to (road, sky, person). It says which class, not which object: touching objects of one class merge into one region, and the map cannot tell how many there are. Telling apart the objects of one class is instance segmentation. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (slide 7).

body.zh: 和图像一样大的一张图，每格是那一点离相机的距离，例如以米计。它是三维恢复的一种输出，回答「多远」。它的数是长度，可以比较远近、相减；类别图和实例图里的数是编号，不能当距离用。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（三维恢复，幻灯片 7）。
body.en: A map as large as the image whose every cell holds that point's distance from the camera, in metres say. It is one output of 3D reconstruction and answers 'how far'. Its numbers are lengths, which can be compared and subtracted; the numbers in a class map or an instance map are ids and cannot serve as distances. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (3D reconstruction, slide 7).

body.zh: 刻意扰动过的输入：只改动很少的像素，人眼几乎看不出变化，却能让神经网络把一个数字判成另一个数字，或把 dog 判成 hot dog，而且置信度很高。它说明模型在常见的照片上答得好，不等于它对输入的变化鲁棒。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，对抗样本（幻灯片 2–3）。
body.en: An input perturbed on purpose: a few altered pixels, a change the eye hardly sees, make a neural network read one digit as another or a dog as a hot dog, and with high confidence. It shows that answering ordinary photos well does not make a model robust to changes in its input. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, adversarial examples (slides 2–3).

body.zh: 已知物体、材质、灯光和相机，向前生成一张图像：这是正问题。计算机视觉走反方向，从图像推测这些东西。实际系统常把两者放在一起：按当前的估计渲染一张预测图，和真实的图比较，再用差异修正估计，叫 render and compare。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉与图形学（幻灯片 8）。
body.en: Given objects, materials, lights and a camera, generate an image forwards: a forward problem. Computer vision goes the other way, inferring these from the image. Real systems often combine the two: render a predicted image from the current estimate, compare it with the real one and correct the estimate by the difference — render and compare. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision and graphics (slide 8).

body.zh: 一个物体挡在另一个前面，被挡住的部分在图像里没有一个像素。它是识别难的原因之一：同一个物体露出的部分不同，看上去就不同。被整个挡住的东西，图像既不能证实，也不能否定，连「它不在场景里」也说不出。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，识别为什么难（幻灯片 28）。
body.en: One object stands in front of another, and the hidden part has no pixel at all in the image. It is one reason recognition is hard: one object looks different depending on what part of it shows. Of something entirely hidden the image can confirm nothing and deny nothing — not even that it is absent from the scene. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, why recognition is hard (slide 28).

body.zh: 数字图像的一格。灰度图里一个像素是一个数，说那里有多亮；彩色图里是几个数，每个通道一个。像素只记下亮度和颜色，不记下这一点离相机多远。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，成像与图像张量（幻灯片 8、22）。
body.en: One cell of a digital image. In a greyscale image a pixel is one number, how bright that place is; in a colour image it is several numbers, one per channel. A pixel records brightness and colour, not how far that point is from the camera. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, image formation and the image tensor (slides 8, 22).

body.zh: 彩色图比灰度图多出的那一维：每个像素按通道存几个数，最常见的是红、绿、蓝三个。三个通道是相机和人眼视觉的工程表示（人眼有三类主要的视锥细胞），不是说自然界只有三种颜色。取出一个通道，得到的是一张灰度图。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，图像张量（幻灯片 22）。
body.en: The axis a colour image has beyond a greyscale one: each pixel stores one number per channel, most often three, for red, green and blue. Three channels are an engineering representation shared by cameras and human vision (the eye has three main kinds of cone), not a claim that nature has only three colours. One channel taken out is a greyscale image. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the image tensor (slide 22).

body.zh: 常用的开源计算机视觉库，Python 里写作 cv2。用它时要记住它自己的约定：尺寸写成 (宽, 高)，和 NumPy 数组的形状 (高, 宽, 通道) 相反；cv2.imread 读进来的彩色图按 BGR 排通道；缩放的插值方式有 INTER_NEAREST、INTER_LINEAR 等。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲与 workshop 2。
body.en: A widely used open-source computer vision library, cv2 in Python. Its own conventions must be kept in mind: a size is written (width, height), the reverse of a NumPy array's shape (height, width, channels); cv2.imread reads colour images with their channels in BGR order; its resizing interpolations include INTER_NEAREST and INTER_LINEAR. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 and workshop 2.

body.zh: 针孔相机里光线穿过针孔后落上的平面，讲义也叫成像平面；它离针孔的距离是焦距 f。真实相机的传感器在针孔后面，像是倒的；讲义把像平面画在针孔前面，像不倒过来，也省掉负号。这是坐标约定，不是传感器真正的位置。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与成像模型（幻灯片 11、18）。
body.en: The plane that rays reach after passing a pinhole camera's hole, at the focal length f from it. In a real camera the sensor is behind the hole and the image is upside down; the lectures draw the image plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright and the minus signs go away. This is a coordinate convention, not where the sensor really is. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and the image formation model (slides 11, 18).

body.zh: 针孔相机里是针孔到像平面的距离 f，透镜相机里是镜头的焦距。它管像的大小，和管进光量的光圈直径是两个不同的长度，不能混为一谈。像平面上它以毫米计，在数字图像里常换成以像素计。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与透镜（幻灯片 11、13）。
body.en: In a pinhole camera, the distance f from the hole to the image plane; in a lens camera, the lens's focal length. It sets the image size and is a different length from the aperture diameter, which sets the light; the two are not to be confused. On the image plane it is in millimetres; for digital images it is often converted to pixels. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and lenses (slides 11, 13).

body.zh: 镜头放光进来的开口，大小用直径 D 表示（台上记作 A）。它管进来多少光；管像的大小的是焦距。光圈小，接近针孔，进光少；光圈大，进光多。摄影上用 f 数写光圈。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，透镜与光圈（幻灯片 13、16）。
body.en: The opening through which a lens lets light in, its size given as the diameter D (A on the bench). It sets how much light comes in; the image size is the focal length's business. A small aperture comes close to a pinhole and lets in little light; a large one lets in more. Photography writes the aperture as an f-number. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, lens and aperture (slides 13, 16).

body.zh: 一点射出的光经过透镜，在传感器上落成的那个小圆，也叫弥散圆。点在对焦距离上时，它缩成一点；不在时，它有一定大小，这一点就显得糊。模糊圈小于一个门槛（比如一个像素的大小）时，就算清晰。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，相机为什么需要透镜（幻灯片 12–13）。
body.en: The small disc that the light from one point makes on the sensor after the lens, also called the circle of confusion. For a point at the focus distance it shrinks to a point; otherwise it has some size and the point looks blurred. A blur circle below a threshold, such as one pixel's size, counts as sharp. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, why cameras need lenses (slides 12–13).

body.zh: 摄影上写光圈的方式：f 数 = 焦距 / 光圈直径，写成 f/2、f/5.6、f/32。同一支镜头，f 数越大，光圈越小。70 mm 镜头在 f/5.6 时，光圈直径约为 70/5.6 = 12.5 mm。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，光圈与景深（幻灯片 16）。
body.en: Photography's way of writing the aperture: f-number = focal length / aperture diameter, written f/2, f/5.6, f/32. On one lens, the larger the f-number, the smaller the aperture. A 70 mm lens at f/5.6 has an aperture about 70/5.6 = 12.5 mm across. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, aperture and depth of field (slide 16).

body.zh: 光轴穿过像平面的那一点，像平面上量位置的起点。理想相机的主点在传感器正中，视场两边对称；真实相机的主点会有偏移，要和像素尺寸、镜头畸变一起考虑。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与焦距（幻灯片 11、15）。
body.en: The point where the optical axis meets the image plane, from which positions on the plane are measured. In an ideal camera it sits at the centre of the sensor and the field of view is symmetric; in a real camera it is offset and must be accounted for along with the pixel size and lens distortion. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and focal length (slides 11, 15).

body.zh: Python 的绘图库。matplotlib.pyplot.imshow 按 RGB 显示彩色图，所以 OpenCV 读进来的 BGR 图要先用 cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB) 换通道顺序再显示；这一步只换顺序，不改内容和尺寸。出处：COMP90086 workshop 2。
body.en: Python's plotting library. matplotlib.pyplot.imshow displays colour images as RGB, so a BGR image read by OpenCV is first converted with cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB); this changes only the channel order, not the content or the size. Source: COMP90086 workshop 2.

body.zh: 无符号 8 位整数，像素最常见的存法：每个值是 0 到 255 的整数，黑是 0，白是 255，RGB 里的纯红是 [255, 0, 0]。相加、相乘容易溢出，所以处理时常换成 float32 并缩到 [0, 1]，算完再明确地换回去。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，数据类型（幻灯片 26）与 workshop 2。
body.en: The unsigned 8-bit integer, the commonest way to store pixels: each value a whole number from 0 to 255, black 0, white 255, pure red in RGB [255, 0, 0]. Sums and products overflow easily, so processing often converts to float32 scaled to [0, 1] and casts back explicitly at the end. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, data types (slide 26), and workshop 2.

body.zh: Python 的数组库。图像在里面是一个数组，形状写成 (高, 宽, 通道)，下标先行后列：image[y, x]。切片 image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w] 取出一块；切片返回的常是原数组的视图，要单独修改时先 .copy()。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲与 workshop 2。
body.en: Python's array library. An image is an array whose shape is written (height, width, channels), indexed row first: image[y, x]. The slice image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w] takes out a region; a slice is often a view of the original array, so copy it with .copy() before changing it on its own. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 and workshop 2.

body.zh: 图的宽与高之比。把 768×512 直接压成 512×512 会改变宽高比，物体变胖或变瘦；要保持比例，宽和高乘同一个比例（缩到约 512×341），要的形状再用裁剪取出。OpenCV 的尺寸写成 (宽, 高)，NumPy 的形状是 (高, 宽, 通道)，两者不能照搬。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 34）与 workshop 2。
body.en: An image's width over its height. Squashing 768×512 straight into 512×512 changes it, and objects grow fatter or thinner; to keep proportions, scale width and height by one factor (to about 512×341) and take the wanted shape with a crop. OpenCV writes a size as (width, height) while a NumPy shape is (height, width, channels); one cannot be passed as the other. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 34) and workshop 2.

body.zh: 图的宽与高之比。把 768×512 直接压成 512×512 会改变宽高比，物体变胖或变瘦；要保持比例，宽和高乘同一个比例（约 768×512 → 768 · 2/3 × 512 · 2/3），要的形状再用裁剪取出。OpenCV 的尺寸写成 (宽, 高)，NumPy 的形状是 (高, 宽, 通道)，不能照搬。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 34）与 workshop 2。
body.en: An image's width over its height. Squashing 768×512 straight into 512×512 changes it, and objects grow fatter or thinner; to keep proportions, scale width and height by one factor and take the wanted shape with a crop. OpenCV writes a size as (width, height) while a NumPy shape is (height, width, channels); one cannot be passed as the other. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 34) and workshop 2.

why: Copy step, chapter 0: each intro says where the station is stuck, the level's question, what is given and what counts as right; pass texts name the term and its neighbours; the lede no longer promises translation

value.zh: 先弄清一张图能回答什么，再从一格格的数起步，搭出相机模型和读图、缩放、量化、裁剪的电路：场景怎样变成一组数，这组数又怎样被处理。
value.en: First learn what one image can answer; then, starting from cells of numbers, build camera models and circuits that read, resize, quantise and crop images: how a scene becomes an array of numbers, and how that array is handled.

ops.zh: 整台机器从一台视觉检查台起步。它不会计算，也碰不到一个像素：它只看图，读别的视觉系统交出的输出，判断哪一份回答了请求。同一张图上能提的问题不止一种，每种问题要的输出形式也不一样。
ops.en: The whole machine starts as a vision test station. It computes nothing and cannot touch a single pixel: it looks at the image, reads the outputs other vision systems hand in, and judges which of them answers a request. One image can be asked many kinds of question, and each kind needs its own form of output.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：图里有哪些物体、它们在哪里，一个答案至少要带上哪些信息？每一轮有两个问题和三份输出，每份输出照原样写出它说了什么。为每个问题选出刚好够回答它的那一份：缺了信息不够，多带了不需要的也不算刚好。
ops.en: This level asks: which objects are in the image and where are they — what must an answer contain at the least? Each round has two questions and three outputs, each written out exactly as it was handed in. Give every question the output that is just enough to answer it: an output missing something falls short, and one carrying more than is needed is not just enough either.

ops.zh: 每个物体一个类别加一个<wiki-ref to="bounding-box"></wiki-ref>，是<wiki-ref to="detection"></wiki-ref>的输出；只给类别的是<wiki-ref to="classification"></wiki-ref>，不说位置。
ops.en: A class and a <wiki-ref to="bounding-box"></wiki-ref> for each object is the output of <wiki-ref to="detection"></wiki-ref>; a class alone is <wiki-ref to="classification"></wiki-ref>, which says nothing of position.

ops.zh: 检测框只把物体圈在一个矩形里，说不出框里哪些像素属于物体。有的输出给每个像素一个数，是一张和照片一样大的图：0 是背景，其余的数是什么意思，要对照画面读出来。
ops.en: A detection box only rings an object with a rectangle and cannot say which pixels inside it belong to the object. Some outputs give every pixel a number, a map as large as the photo: 0 is background, and what the other numbers mean has to be read against the picture.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：「每个像素属于哪一类」和「每个像素属于哪一个物体」是同一个问题吗？每一轮有两个问题和几张逐像素图，图名不说它是哪一种。为每个问题选出刚好够回答它的那张。
ops.en: This level asks: is 'which class does each pixel belong to' the same question as 'which object does each pixel belong to'? Each round has two questions and a few per-pixel maps whose names do not say what kind they are. Give every question the map that is just enough to answer it.

ops.zh: 每个像素标出属于哪一个物体，是<wiki-ref to="instance-segmentation"></wiki-ref>；只标类别，是<wiki-ref to="semantic-segmentation"></wiki-ref>。
ops.en: Labelling each pixel with its object is <wiki-ref to="instance-segmentation"></wiki-ref>; labelling only its class is <wiki-ref to="semantic-segmentation"></wiki-ref>.

ops.zh: 到这里，请求问的都是类别和位置。一辆车上的视觉系统同时交出五份输出：一个标签、一组检测框和三张逐像素图。车上各个模块的请求由检查台分给它们，其中一个请求问的是距离。
ops.en: So far every request has asked about classes and positions. The vision system on a car hands in five outputs at once: a label, a set of detection boxes and three per-pixel maps. The station routes the requests of the car's modules to them, and one request asks about distance.

ops.zh: 这一关新在两处：一个请求可以有几份够用的输出，选出够用的都算对；三张图的格子里都是数，含义却不同，要对照画面读出来。这一关的问题是：「那辆车离我多远」该由哪一份回答？类别图里的数能当距离用吗？
ops.en: Two things are new here: a request may have several sufficient outputs, and choosing those that suffice is right; and the three maps all hold numbers that mean different things, to be read against the picture. This level asks: which output answers 'how far away is that car'? Can the numbers in a class map serve as distances?

ops.zh: 三张图的格子里都是数：对照图里的物体，判断每张图的数是编号、类别还是长度。
ops.en: All three maps hold numbers: compare them with the objects in the picture and decide whether each map's numbers are ids, classes or lengths.

after.zh: 每格是一个距离的图叫<wiki-ref to="depth-map"></wiki-ref>，是三维恢复的输出；类别输出里的数是编号，回答不了「多远」。
after.en: A map whose every cell is a distance is a <wiki-ref to="depth-map"></wiki-ref>, an output of 3D reconstruction; the numbers in a class output are ids and cannot answer 'how far'.

ops.zh: 检查台会比较输出和请求了，可识别还要回答「这是不是同一个东西」，而同一个物体换个角度、换盏灯，拍出的像素就全变了。检查台旁边多了一个受控的小场景：一个物体、一架能绕着它转的相机和一盏灯。场景渲出的图，可以拿来和候选图比较。
ops.en: The station can now compare outputs with requests, but recognition must also say whether two pictures show the same thing, and one object seen from another angle or under another lamp gives entirely different pixels. Beside the station there is now a small controlled scene: one object, a camera that orbits it and a lamp. What the scene renders can be compared with the candidates.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：两张图的像素几乎都不同，拍的会是同一个物体吗？参照图拍的是场景里的那个物体。第一个任务只能转相机，第二个任务只能移灯；每一轮选出拍的也是它的全部候选图，一张不多，一张不少。
ops.en: This level asks: when two pictures differ in almost every pixel, can they show the same object? The reference shows the object in the scene. In the first task only the camera turns, in the second only the lamp moves; in each round choose every candidate that shows that object too, no more and no fewer.

ops.zh: 同一个物体换视角、换光照，像素几乎全变，这是<wiki-ref to="intra-class-variation"></wiki-ref>：识别要容忍它，不能靠记住像素。
ops.en: One object under another viewpoint or light changes nearly every pixel: this is <wiki-ref to="intra-class-variation"></wiki-ref>, which recognition must tolerate instead of memorising pixels.

ops.zh: 检查台看出了同一个物体能拍成很不一样的图。一个分类器面对这些变化能不能照样认对，要靠检验。它的作者说：「它在任何背景下都认得出猫。」检查台拿到几批样例，每个样例写着人工标注的类别、背景、分类器的预测和置信度。
ops.en: The station has seen that one object can be photographed very differently. Whether a classifier still answers right through such changes has to be tested. Its author claims: 'it recognises a cat against any background.' The station receives a few batches of cases, each listing the labelled class, the background, the classifier's prediction and its confidence.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：分类器在一张照片上答对了，而且很有把握，这能说明它换了背景也认得出吗？每一批选出一个能推翻这句话的样例；一个也没有时，选「没有」。
ops.en: This level asks: when a classifier gets one photo right, and confidently, does that show it will recognise the cat against other backgrounds? In each batch choose a case that refutes the claim; when there is none, choose 'none'.

ops.zh: 无关变化下输出仍可靠，叫<wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>：一个反例就能推翻它；只改几个像素的<wiki-ref to="adversarial-example"></wiki-ref>也是反例。
ops.en: An output that stays reliable through irrelevant change shows <wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>; one counterexample refutes it, and an <wiki-ref to="adversarial-example"></wiki-ref>, a few pixels changed, is one too.

ops.zh: 在<level-ref to="0B2"></level-ref>里，检查台检验的是别人的论断，样例是现成的。这一关方向反过来：由检查台替一个杯子分类器设计检验，从一批拍杯子的样例里挑出一组测试集。
ops.en: In <level-ref to="0B2"></level-ref> the station judged someone else's claim against cases already given. This level turns the other way: the station designs the test for a mug classifier, picking a test set out of a batch of photos of a mug.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：要检验它的<wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>，测试集里该放哪些样例？看每张样例和一张普通的正面照比变了什么：视角、光照，还是有东西挡在杯子前面。选出的一组要把这三种变化都覆盖到。
ops.en: This level asks: to test its <wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>, which cases belong in the test set? See what each case changes against a plain front view: the viewpoint, the light, or something standing in front of the mug. The set you choose must cover all three changes.

ops.zh: 选出一组样例，让它覆盖换视角、换光照和有东西挡在前面三种变化。
ops.en: Choose a set of cases that covers a changed viewpoint, changed lighting and something standing in front.

ops.zh: 到这里，检查台默认答案就在图里。可图是由场景生成的：<wiki-ref to="computer-graphics"></wiki-ref>从物体、材质、光照和相机出发，正向渲出图像；视觉走反方向，手里只有图，要说出场景是什么样。
ops.en: So far the station has assumed the answer is in the image. But images are generated from scenes: <wiki-ref to="computer-graphics"></wiki-ref> renders an image forwards from objects, materials, light and a camera; vision goes the other way, holding only the image and having to say what the scene is like.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：只看这一张图，红色箱子离相机多远？题目给出这张图和几个都渲得出它的候选场景，判断关于场景的每句话：在每个候选场景里都对，才算成立；都错是不成立；有对有错就是无法确定。
ops.en: This level asks: from this image alone, how far is the red box from the camera? You get the image and several candidate scenes that all render it, and judge each statement about the scene: true in every candidate, it holds; false in every one, it does not; true in some and false in others, it is undetermined.

ops.zh: 从图像推回场景是<wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>：三维投成二维丢了一维，不同的场景能渲出同一张图。
ops.en: Inferring the scene from the image is an <wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>: projecting 3D to 2D loses a dimension, and different scenes can render the same image.

ops.zh: 在<level-ref to="0C1"></level-ref>里，图上看得见的东西也可能有几种解释。这一关场景里立着一块不透明的灰色挡板，挡住了它后面的东西：被<wiki-ref to="occlusion"></wiki-ref>的部分，图里一个像素也没有。题目照样给出一张图和几个都渲得出它的候选场景。
ops.en: In <level-ref to="0C1"></level-ref> even what the image shows allowed several explanations. Here an opaque grey screen stands in the scene and hides what is behind it: a part lost to <wiki-ref to="occlusion"></wiki-ref> has not one pixel in the image. As before you get the image and several candidate scenes that all render it.

ops.zh: 这一关新在看不见的东西：图里看不到的，图像能说明它是什么吗？关于看得见的物体和关于挡板后面的话，都按候选场景判断，每个场景里都对才算成立，每个场景里都错才算不成立。
ops.en: What is new is the unseen: can an image say what something it does not show is? Statements about the visible objects and about what is behind the screen are judged alike against the candidate scenes: true in every one, they hold; false in every one, they do not.

ops.zh: 检查台会判断一份输出够不够回答请求，会找反例，也知道一张图说明不了什么。这一关把三样放进一个应用：一台救援机器人在倒塌的楼里找人，找到一个就要靠过去。它的视觉系统交出什么、怎样检验、哪些问题单凭一张图答不了，都由检查台来定。
ops.en: The station can judge whether an output answers a request, find counterexamples, and tell what one image cannot settle. This level puts the three into one application: a rescue robot searches a collapsed building and must go to each person it finds. What its vision system hands in, how that is tested and which questions one image cannot answer are all for the station to decide.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：机器人要找到每个人并靠过去，它的视觉输出要包含什么，又该怎样检验？三个任务依次是：为请求选输出，为每种预测配上检验它的参照，再判断几句关于现场的话。新的一点是：输出要包含什么，由机器人接下来要做的动作决定。
ops.en: This level asks: a rescue robot must find every person and go to them — what must its vision output contain, and how should it be tested? The three tasks: choose outputs for the requests, pair each kind of prediction with a reference that tests it, then judge a few statements about the site. What is new: the robot's next action decides what the output must contain.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：机器人要找到每个人并靠过去，它的视觉输出要包含什么，又该怎样检验？一共三步：选输出，配检验用的参照，再判断几句关于现场的话。
value.en: This level asks: a robot must find every person and go to them — what must its vision output contain, and how should it be tested? There are three steps: choose the outputs, pair them with references to test against, then judge statements about the site.

value.zh: 检查台要正式上岗了：一台救援机器人在倒塌的楼里找人，找到一个就要靠过去。它的视觉系统交出什么、怎样检验、哪些问题一张图答不了，都由检查台来定。
value.en: The station goes to work: a rescue robot searches a collapsed building for people and must go to each one it finds. What its vision system hands in, how that is tested, and which questions one image cannot answer are the station's to settle.

value.zh: 这一关要回答的是：图里看不到的东西，图像能说明它是什么吗？关于看得见的物体和关于挡板后面的话，都按候选场景判断。
value.en: This level asks: can an image say what something it does not show is? Judge the statements about the visible objects and about what is behind the screen, by the candidate scenes alike.

value.zh: 场景里立着一块不透明的灰色挡板，挡住了它后面的东西。检查台照样拿到一张图和几个都渲得出这张图的候选场景。
value.en: An opaque grey screen stands in the scene and hides what is behind it. The station again gets one image and several candidate scenes that all render it.

value.zh: 从图像推回场景是<wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>：不同的场景能渲出同一张图。
value.en: Going from the image back to the scene is an <wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>: different scenes can render the same image.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：只看这一张图，红色箱子离相机多远？几个候选场景都渲得出这张图。一句话在每个候选场景里都对，才算成立；都错是不成立；有对有错就是无法确定。
value.en: This level asks: from this image alone, how far is the red box from the camera? Several candidate scenes all render this image. A statement true in every candidate holds, false in every one does not hold, and true in some, false in others is undetermined.

value.zh: 图形学从物体、光照和相机出发，正向渲出一张图。检查台面对的是反方向：手里只有图，要说出场景是什么样。
value.en: Graphics starts from objects, light and a camera and renders an image forwards. The station faces the other way: it holds only the image and must say what the scene is like.

value.zh: 选出一组样例，让它覆盖换视角、换光照和有遮挡三种变化。
value.en: Choose a set of cases that covers a changed viewpoint, changed lighting and occlusion.

value.zh: 要检验它对无关变化是否鲁棒，测试集里该放哪些样例？看每张样例和第一张比变了什么：视角、光照，还是有东西挡在前面。选出的一组要把这三种变化都覆盖到。
value.en: To test whether it is robust to irrelevant change, which cases belong in the set? Look at what each photo changes against the first: the viewpoint, the light, or something standing in front. The set you choose must cover all three changes.

value.zh: 这次检查台不判断别人的论断，而是替一个杯子分类器设计检验：从一批拍杯子的样例里挑出一组测试。
value.en: This time the station does not judge someone's claim; it designs the test for a mug classifier, picking a test set out of a batch of photos of a mug.

value.zh: 输入有无关的变化时输出仍然可靠，叫<wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>：答对一次证明不了，一个反例就能推翻。
value.en: Staying reliable when irrelevant things about the input change is <wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>: one right answer cannot prove it, one counterexample refutes it.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：分类器在一张照片上答对了，而且很有把握，这能说明它换了背景也认得出吗？选出一个能推翻这句话的样例；一个也没有时，选「没有」。
value.en: This level asks: when a classifier gets one photo right, and confidently, does that show it will recognise the cat against other backgrounds? Choose a case that refutes the claim; when there is none, choose 'none'.

value.zh: 一个分类器的作者说：「它在任何背景下都认得出猫。」检查台拿到一批样例，每个样例有人工标注的真实类别和分类器的预测，还有预测的置信度。
value.en: The author of a classifier claims: 'it recognises a cat against any background.' The station receives a batch of cases, each with its labelled true class, the classifier's prediction and the confidence of that prediction.

value.zh: 同一个物体换个视角、换盏灯，像素几乎全变，这叫<wiki-ref to="intra-class-variation"></wiki-ref>。
value.en: One object seen from another angle or under another light changes nearly every pixel: this is <wiki-ref to="intra-class-variation"></wiki-ref>.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：两张图的像素几乎都不同，拍的会是同一个物体吗？参照图拍的是场景里的物体；选出所有拍的也是它的候选图。
value.en: This level asks: when two pictures differ in almost every pixel, can they show the same object? The reference shows the object in the scene; choose every candidate that shows it too.

value.zh: 检查台旁边多了一个受控的小场景：一个物体、一架能绕着它转的相机和一盏灯。场景渲出的每张图，你都可以拿来和候选图比。
value.en: Beside the station there is now a small controlled scene: one object, a camera that orbits it and a lamp. Every picture the scene renders can be compared with the candidates.

t.zh: 到这里，请求问的都是类别和位置。一辆车上的视觉系统同时交出五份输出：一个标签、一组检测框和三张逐像素图。车上各个模块的请求由检查台分给它们，其中一个请求问的是距离。
t.en: So far every request has asked about classes and positions. The vision system on a car hands in five outputs at once: a label, a set of detection boxes and three per-pixel maps. The station routes the requests of the car's modules to them, and one request asks about distance.

t.zh: 这一关新在两处：一个请求可以有几份够用的输出，选出够用的都算对；三张图的格子里都是数，含义却不同，要对照画面读出来。这一关的问题是：「那辆车离我多远」该由哪一份回答？类别图里的数能当距离用吗？
t.en: Two things are new here: a request may have several sufficient outputs, and choosing those that suffice is right; and the three maps all hold numbers that mean different things, to be read against the picture. This level asks: which output answers 'how far away is that car'? Can the numbers in a class map serve as distances?

brief.zh: 为每个请求选出能回答它的输出，够用的都可以选。
brief.en: For each request, choose outputs that answer it; any that suffice may be chosen.

hint.zh: 三张图的格子里都是数：对照图里的物体，判断每张图的数是编号、类别还是长度。
hint.en: All three maps hold numbers: compare them with the objects in the picture and decide whether each map's numbers are ids, classes or lengths.

prompt.zh: 路面是哪些像素？
prompt.en: Which pixels are road?

prompt.zh: 每个行人各在哪里？
prompt.en: Where is each pedestrian?

prompt.zh: 第 2 行第 4 列那个像素处的车，离相机多远？
prompt.en: How far from the camera is the car at row 2, column 4?

prompt.zh: 最近的那面墙离相机多远？
prompt.en: How far from the camera is the nearest wall?

prompt.zh: 停着几辆车？
prompt.en: How many cars are parked?

prompt.zh: 画面里有行人吗？
prompt.en: Is there a pedestrian in the picture?

value.zh: 三张图的格子里都是数：对照图里的物体，猜出每张图的数是编号、类别还是长度。
value.en: All three maps hold numbers: compare them with the scene and work out whether each map's numbers are ids, classes or lengths.

value.zh: 和前面不同，这里一个请求可以有几份够用的输出，选出其中任何够用的都算对。要看清的是每份输出里的数是什么意思、以什么为单位：「那辆车离我多远」该由哪一份回答？
value.en: Unlike before, a request may have several sufficient outputs, and choosing any that suffice is right. What matters is what the numbers in each output mean, and in what unit: which output answers 'how far away is that car'?

value.zh: 一辆车上的视觉系统同时交出五份输出：一个标签、一组框和三张逐像素图。检查台要把车上各个模块的请求分给它们。
value.en: The vision system on a car hands in five outputs at once: a label, a set of boxes and three per-pixel maps. The station must route the requests of the car's modules to them.

value.zh: 给每个像素标出它属于哪一个物体，叫<wiki-ref to="instance-segmentation"></wiki-ref>；只标类别的是语义分割。
value.en: Labelling each pixel with the object it belongs to is <wiki-ref to="instance-segmentation"></wiki-ref>; labelling only the class is semantic segmentation.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：「每个像素属于哪一类」和「每个像素属于哪一个物体」是同一个问题吗？对着每张图里的数，为每个问题选出刚好够回答它的那张。
value.en: This level asks: is 'which class does each pixel belong to' the same question as 'which object does each pixel belong to'? Reading the numbers in each map, give every question the map that is just enough to answer it.

value.zh: 有的输出不止给一个框，而是给每个像素一个数：一张和照片一样大的图。0 是背景，其余的数是什么意思，要从图里读出来。
value.en: Some outputs give not a box but a number for every pixel: a map as large as the photo. 0 is background; what the other numbers mean has to be read from the map.

value.zh: 给出每个物体的类别和框，这样的输出是<wiki-ref to="detection"></wiki-ref>的结果；只给类别是分类。
value.en: An output that gives each object a class and a box is the result of <wiki-ref to="detection"></wiki-ref>; a class alone is classification.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：图里有哪些物体、它们在哪里，一个答案至少要带上哪些信息？读每份输出里写了什么，为每个问题选出够回答它、又不多带东西的那一份。
value.en: This level asks: which objects are in the picture and where are they — what must an answer contain at the least? Read what each output says, and give every question the output that answers it without carrying anything more.

value.zh: 检查台收到一张照片和几个关于它的问题。它自己不会看图，只能从几份现成的输出里挑：每份输出是某个视觉系统交出的答案。
value.en: The test station receives a photo and a few questions about it. It cannot look at the photo itself; it can only choose among ready-made outputs, each the answer some vision system handed in.

value.zh: 从一格一格的数出发，搭出读图、移图、缩放的电路，再用相机模型解释图从哪里来。
value.en: Start from a grid of numbers, wire circuits that read, move and resize images, and explain with a camera model where an image comes from.

why: Copy step, chapter 1: the era's first level says what the workbench adds and why the station is not enough; each intro says what the machine lacks, the question, the givens and what counts as right; new parts named after their need; no claim of a first circuit in one of three parallel branches; pass texts name each term with its neighbours and library names

ops.zh: 检查台能判断答案，却说不出图里的数从哪里来，也读不了、改不了、算不了一个像素。这一章给它装上相机与图像工作台：先弄清一张图怎样存成数，再搭相机模型和处理图像的电路。
ops.en: The station could judge answers but could not say where an image's numbers come from, nor read, change or compute a single pixel. This chapter gives it a camera and image workbench: first how an image is stored as numbers, then camera models and circuits that process images.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：相机拍下的这张小图，存进计算机是什么样子？画面旁边是一张空格子，行数和列数由你填出的样子决定。灰度图里每个<wiki-ref to="pixel"></wiki-ref>是一个数：0 是黑，1 是白，中间是不同深浅的灰。照着画面填，形状和每个数都对才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: what does this small picture from the camera look like once it is stored in the computer? Beside the picture is an empty grid whose rows and columns are whatever you fill in. In a grey image each <wiki-ref to="pixel"></wiki-ref> is one number: 0 is black, 1 is white, and the numbers between are shades of grey. Fill it from the picture; it is right when the shape and every number are.

ops.zh: 彩色图多一维<wiki-ref to="channel"></wiki-ref>：每个像素存三个数 (R, G, B)，说红、绿、蓝各有多亮，各在 0 到 1 之间。
ops.en: A colour image has one more axis, the <wiki-ref to="channel"></wiki-ref>: each pixel stores three numbers (R, G, B), how bright its red, green and blue are, each from 0 to 1.

ops.zh: 灰度图存成 高 × 宽 的<wiki-ref to="image-array"></wiki-ref>，彩色图再多一维通道：高 × 宽 × 3。像素只说多亮，不说多远。
ops.en: A grey image is stored as a height × width <wiki-ref to="image-array"></wiki-ref>, a colour image with one more axis for channels: height × width × 3. A pixel says how bright, not how far.

ops.zh: 数存好了，要读写其中一个像素，先得说清是哪一个。工作台给图上的每一格一对坐标 (x, y)，格子旁边画着两条坐标轴。
ops.en: The numbers are stored; to read or write one pixel, one must first say which. The workbench gives every cell of an image a pair of coordinates (x, y) and draws the two axes beside the grid.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：图像坐标 (x, y) 指的是哪一个像素？前两个任务对着坐标轴点出给定坐标的格子，其中一张图宽高不等；第三个任务反过来，写出高亮格子的坐标。点中或写对那一格才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: which pixel do image coordinates (x, y) refer to? The first two tasks have you pick the cell at given coordinates by the axes, one of them on an image whose width and height differ; the third goes the other way and asks for the coordinates of a highlighted cell. Only the right cell counts.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="pixel-coordinates"></wiki-ref>：原点在左上角，从 0 数起，y 向下增大，和数学课上 y 轴朝上的坐标不同。
ops.en: These are <wiki-ref to="pixel-coordinates"></wiki-ref>: the origin at the top-left corner, counting from 0, y growing downwards, unlike the upward y of school geometry.

ops.zh: <level-ref to="1A2"></level-ref>用的是坐标 (x, y)，程序里读像素用的却是数组下标 I[第几行, 第几列]。两种写法说的是同一批像素，顺序不一样。
ops.en: <level-ref to="1A2"></level-ref> used coordinates (x, y), but a program reads a pixel by its array index I[row, column]. The two name the same pixels in a different order.

ops.zh: 这一关新在方向：从坐标换到数组。先按下标点出像素，再从数组的形状读出图的宽和高，最后把<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>给出的尺寸写成数组形状；OpenCV 把尺寸写成 (宽, 高)。每一问都要点中那一格或写对那两个数。
ops.en: What is new is the direction: from coordinates to arrays. Pick a pixel by its index, read an image's width and height off its array shape, then write as an array shape a size given by <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>, which writes sizes as (width, height). Each task wants the right cell or the right two numbers.

ops.zh: 工作台能存、能读像素，却说不出这些数从哪里来：场景里的一点，落到图上的哪个位置？相机台从一台理想的针孔相机起步：一点射出的光穿过针孔，落在离针孔 f 的<wiki-ref to="image-plane"></wiki-ref>上，f 叫<wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref>。台上把像平面画在针孔前面，像是正的。
ops.en: The workbench can store and read pixels but cannot say where the numbers come from: where in the image does a point of the scene land? The camera bench starts with an ideal pinhole camera: light from a point passes the hole and lands on the <wiki-ref to="image-plane"></wiki-ref> at distance f from it, f being the <wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref>. The bench draws the plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：一点穿过针孔，落在像平面的什么位置？同一个物体离得越远，像怎样变？两个任务各只开一个旋钮：先横向移动一点，再前后移动一支箭。像落到圆圈标出的目标上才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: where on the image plane does a point land after passing the hole, and how does the image change as the object moves away? Each of the two tasks opens one knob: first move a point sideways, then move an arrow in depth. It is right when the image lands on the circled target.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="pinhole-projection"></wiki-ref>：像的位置和大小按 f/Z 缩放；讲义把像平面画在针孔前面，只是坐标约定。
ops.en: This is <wiki-ref to="pinhole-projection"></wiki-ref>: where the image lands and how big it is scale with f/Z; drawing the plane in front of the hole is only a coordinate convention.

ops.zh: 在<level-ref to="1B1"></level-ref>里，像的大小靠移动物体来改。这一关物体和它的距离都锁住了：物体不动、相机不挪，还有什么能让像变大？
ops.en: In <level-ref to="1B1"></level-ref> the image size changed when the object moved. Here the object and its distance are locked: with neither the object nor the camera moving, what else can make the image larger?

ops.zh: 这一关新在改相机，不改场景：台上只有<wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref> f 能动。先在台上让像高达到目标；再不上台，为另外两组数算出 f；最后拿其中一组上台验证，像高等于目标才算对。
ops.en: What is new is changing the camera instead of the scene: only the <wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref> f turns. First bring the image to the target height on the bench; then work out f for two other sets of numbers without it; finally check one of them on the bench, where the image must match the target.

ops.zh: 到这里，任务都是由物体求像。这一关反过来问：看到像有多高，能定出物体有多远吗？焦距固定为 f = 2。每一轮给出几组（物高, 距离），选出像高都是 1、距离又各不相同的那几组，全部选对、一组不多才算对。
ops.en: So far every task has gone from the object to its image. This level asks the other way: does the height of an image tell how far away the object is? The focal length is fixed at f = 2. Each round lists several (height, depth) pairs; choose those that all image 1 tall at different depths, all of them and no others.

after.zh: 像只定出物高和距离的比 H/Z：大而远和小而近成同一个像，这是<wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>在相机上的样子。
after.en: An image fixes only the ratio H/Z: large-and-far and small-and-near image alike — the <wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref> as the camera poses it.

ops.zh: 针孔小，进来的光少，图很暗；把孔开大，同一点的光会落到传感器上不同的地方，图就糊。相机台在针孔的位置换上一块焦距 50 mm 的透镜，开两个旋钮：<wiki-ref to="aperture"></wiki-ref>直径 A 管进来多少光，对焦距离是透镜对准的那个距离。
ops.en: A small pinhole lets in little light and the image is dark; widen it and light from one point lands at different places on the sensor, and the image blurs. The camera bench puts a 50 mm lens where the hole was and opens two knobs: the <wiki-ref to="aperture"></wiki-ref> diameter A sets how much light comes in, and the focus distance is the distance the lens is set to.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：要让图更亮又不变糊，只把孔开大够吗？台上有近处的箱子和远处的树。进光量至少要到 4，近处的箱子还要清晰：它在传感器上的<wiki-ref to="blur-circle"></wiki-ref>不超过 0.03 mm。
ops.en: This level asks: to make the image brighter without blurring it, is widening the hole enough? The bench holds a near crate and a far tree. The light must reach at least 4, and the near crate must be sharp: its <wiki-ref to="blur-circle"></wiki-ref> on the sensor no wider than 0.03 mm.

ops.zh: <wiki-ref to="lens"></wiki-ref>让大光圈进来的光重新会聚，但只对对焦距离上的点准，别处成模糊圈；光圈管亮度，焦距管像的大小。
ops.en: A <wiki-ref to="lens"></wiki-ref> brings the light of a wide aperture back together, but only for points at the focus distance; others make blur circles. The aperture sets the light, the focal length the image size.

ops.zh: <level-ref to="1B4"></level-ref>只要一个物体清晰。这一关有两个标记，近处的在 1200 mm，远处的在 2000 mm；透镜对焦在 1500 mm，不能动。光圈这回用摄影的写法给出：<wiki-ref to="f-number"></wiki-ref>是焦距除以光圈直径，50 mm 镜头的 f/2 就是 25 mm 的光圈。
ops.en: <level-ref to="1B4"></level-ref> needed one object sharp. Here there are two markers, the near one at 1200 mm and the far one at 2000 mm; the lens is focused at 1500 mm and stays there. The aperture is now given the photographer's way: the <wiki-ref to="f-number"></wiki-ref> is the focal length over the aperture diameter, so f/2 on a 50 mm lens is a 25 mm aperture.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处两个物体，怎样在一张照片里都清晰？曲线画出每个深度的模糊圈和清晰的门槛。两个标记都清晰、进光量又不低于 1，才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: how can a near and a far object both be sharp in one photo? The curve draws each depth's blur circle against the sharpness threshold. It is right when both markers are sharp and the light is at least 1.

ops.zh: 同时清晰的深度范围叫<wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>：光圈越小、f 数越大，它越深，进来的光也越少。
ops.en: The range of depths sharp at once is the <wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>: the smaller the aperture, the larger the f-number, the deeper it is and the less light comes in.

ops.zh: <level-ref to="1B5"></level-ref>里对焦不能动，只能靠光圈换景深。这一关新在组合：光圈和对焦距离都能动，两个旋钮互相牵制。两个物体在 1000 mm 和 3000 mm，都要清晰，进光量又不能低于 1。这一关的问题是：既要两个深度都清晰，又要足够的光，对焦该放在哪里？
ops.en: In <level-ref to="1B5"></level-ref> the focus was fixed and only the aperture traded depth of field. What is new is the combination: the aperture and the focus distance both turn, and they pull against each other. Two objects stand at 1000 mm and 3000 mm; both must be sharp and the light must not fall below 1. This level asks: with both depths to keep sharp and enough light to gather, where should the focus go?

value.zh: 移动对焦距离时，看曲线低于门槛的那一段跟着往哪里走。
value.en: As the focus distance moves, watch where the stretch of the curve below the threshold goes.

value.zh: 清晰范围在对焦距离的两边都有：对焦在一个物体上时，有一边用不上。
value.en: The sharp range reaches to both sides of the focus: focused on one of the objects, one side goes unused.

ops.zh: 到这里，像平面一直是无限大的，物体的像总能落上去。真正的相机只有一块传感器：相机台装上一块 20 mm 高、200 像素的传感器，<wiki-ref to="principal-point"></wiki-ref>在中心。像落到传感器边外的物体，不在画面里。
ops.en: Until now the image plane has been endless, and every image had somewhere to land. A real camera has only a sensor: the camera bench now holds one 20 mm and 200 pixels tall, its <wiki-ref to="principal-point"></wiki-ref> at the centre. An object whose image falls past its edges is out of the picture.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：要把一排物体全拍进画面，焦距该变长还是变短？三支箭都在 2000 mm 外，台上只有焦距 f 能动。第一个任务要三支都在画面里，中间那支乙又不能太小；第二个任务只拍乙，要它占满画面的高度。
ops.en: This level asks: to get a whole row of objects into the frame, should the focal length grow or shrink? Three arrows stand 2000 mm away, and only the focal length f turns. The first task wants all three in view without the middle arrow B shrinking too far; the second shows B alone and wants it to fill the frame's height.

ops.zh: 焦距决定看得多宽，这是<wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>：传感器一定时，焦距短看得宽，焦距长看得窄、物体显得大。
ops.en: How wide a camera sees is its <wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>: with the sensor fixed, a short focal length sees wide, a long one narrow, with objects looking larger.

ops.zh: 相机台上的长度以毫米计，图里的长度以像素计。这台相机的传感器高 20 mm，竖直方向排着 200 个像素。
ops.en: Lengths on the camera bench are in millimetres, lengths in the image in pixels. This camera's sensor is 20 mm tall and holds 200 pixels from top to bottom.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：物体在图里高 100 像素，实高 120 mm，离相机 600 mm，镜头的焦距是多少毫米？三个任务：先算出焦距，再到相机台上验证，最后写出以像素计的焦距和这台相机竖直方向的<wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>。
ops.en: This level asks: an object is 100 pixels tall in the image, 120 mm tall in reality and 600 mm from the camera — what is the lens's focal length in millimetres? Three tasks: work it out, check it on the camera bench, then give the focal length in pixels and this camera's vertical <wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>.

ops.zh: 物理焦距除以像素尺寸，就是<wiki-ref to="pixel-units"></wiki-ref>：焦距换成图像坐标的单位，视场也能直接用像素算。
ops.en: The physical focal length over the pixel size is the <wiki-ref to="pixel-units"></wiki-ref>: the focal length in the image's own units, from which the field of view follows in pixels.

ops.zh: 工作台读得出一个像素的三个数，却没有问过这三个数各是哪种颜色。一张用<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>读进来的照片在这里显示出来，蓝天成了橙色。这一关的问题是：同一张照片，为什么在这里显示出橙色的天空？
ops.en: The workbench can read a pixel's three numbers but has never asked which colour each one is. A photo read in with <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref> is displayed here, and its blue sky has turned orange. This level asks: why does the same photo show an orange sky here?

ops.zh: 这一关要接一块电路：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。要把一个像素的三个数拆开、重新排，工作台还没有这样的元件。新元件<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出彩色图的一个通道，设成 R、G 或 B，就是每格的第一、第二或第三个数；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图合成一张彩色图。每个像素都和期望相符才算对。
ops.en: This level wires a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Taking a pixel's three numbers apart and putting them back in another order needs parts the workbench lacks. The new part <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes one channel out of a colour image, set to R, G or B, the first, second or third number of each cell; <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> makes three grey images one colour image. It is right when every pixel matches the expected one.

ops.zh: 各个库的<wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>不同：<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>读图得到 BGR，<wiki-ref to="matplotlib"></wiki-ref>按 RGB 显示。
ops.en: Libraries differ in <wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>: <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref> reads images as BGR, <wiki-ref to="matplotlib"></wiki-ref> displays RGB.

ops.zh: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref>弄清了三个数的顺序，还没问它们的大小。电路算出的值可以落在 [0, 1] 之外，屏幕却只显示得出 0 到 1，超出的部分画成最黑或最白。文件里的像素又常存成<wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>：0 到 255 的整数，255 最亮。
ops.en: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref> settled the order of the three numbers but not their size. A circuit may compute values outside [0, 1], while a screen shows only 0 to 1 and draws whatever lies beyond as the darkest or the brightest. And files often store pixels as <wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>: whole numbers from 0 to 255, 255 the brightest.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：两个像素看上去一样白，存着的数一样吗？第一个任务对照每格存着的数，填出它显示出来的值；第二个任务把 OpenCV 读进来的 uint8 像素写成 [0, 1] 里的 (R, G, B)。每格的数都对才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: when two pixels look equally white, do they hold the same number? The first task has you fill in each cell's displayed value from its stored one; the second, write uint8 pixels read by OpenCV as (R, G, B) in [0, 1]. It is right when every cell's numbers are.

ops.zh: 像素值有<wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref>和类型：显示时截到两端，存着的数不变；处理时常把 uint8 换成 [0, 1] 的浮点数。
ops.en: Pixel values have a <wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref> and a type: the display clips to the ends while the stored numbers stay; processing often turns uint8 into floats in [0, 1].

ops.zh: 工作台能读写每个像素，却只能照原样摆放：一张图要放大或缩小，它没有办法。缩放和取出一部分不同，要给新图的每个像素算出一个值；算值之前，先得知道这个像素落在原图的什么位置。
ops.en: The workbench can read and write every pixel, but only where it already is: it cannot enlarge or shrink an image. Unlike taking out a part, resizing computes a value for every pixel of the new image; before any value, it must know where that pixel sits in the original.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：图像放大或缩小时，新图的每个像素对应原图的什么位置？约定是新旧两排像素一样长、像素中心对齐。第一个任务在格子上手算一行，第二个任务搭一块电路，交出整张新图的两张源坐标图，测试的坐标都对才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: when an image is enlarged or shrunk, where in the original does each new pixel sit? The convention: the old and the new row are equally long and pixel centres are aligned. The first task works out one row by hand on the grid; the second wires a circuit that gives the whole new image's two source-coordinate images, right when every tested coordinate is.

t.zh: 手算一行可以，一整张图要每个像素各算一遍，就要电路了：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。新图的每个像素先要有自己的坐标，而手上没有元件能从两个数造出一整张图。
t.en: One row works by hand; a whole image, every pixel worked out, needs a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Each new pixel first needs its own coordinates, and no part in hand makes a whole image out of two numbers.

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref>给定宽和高，给出每格就是自己 x、y 的两张坐标图。坐标还要换算：<part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref>给出一个固定的数，<part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref>对数和整张图逐个值地算。
t.en: The new part <part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref> takes a width and a height and gives the two coordinate images whose cells hold their own x and y. The coordinates still need converting: <part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref> gives a fixed number, and <part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>, <part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref> and <part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref> work value by value on numbers and whole images.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>：每个新像素反向映射回原图，不把旧像素正向搬过去；各个库的对齐约定不同，要写明。
ops.en: This is a <wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>: each new pixel mapped back into the original, not old pixels pushed forwards; libraries align differently, so the convention must be stated.

ops.zh: 有了<part-ref to="sampleGrid"></part-ref>，每个新像素都知道自己落在原图的哪里；可这个位置一般不是整数，原图在那里没有像素。手上的元件只在同一个位置上算，没有一个能把原图某处的值搬到新图上。
ops.en: With the <part-ref to="sampleGrid"></part-ref> every new pixel knows where it sits in the original; but that position is seldom a whole number, and the original has no pixel there. The parts in hand compute in place, and none can carry a value from somewhere in the original to the new image.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：放大一张图时，落在两个旧像素之间的新像素，值从哪里来？新元件<part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref>按整数坐标在图上取值，<part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref>读出图的宽高，<part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref>把连续的数变成整数。离两边一样远时，约定取坐标较大的一边。输出图逐格和期望相符才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: when an image is enlarged, where does a new pixel that falls between two old ones get its value? New parts: <part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref> reads an image at whole-number coordinates, <part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref> gives an image's width and height, and <part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref> turns a continuous number into a whole one. When a position is equally far from two pixels, the convention takes the larger coordinate. It is right when the output matches the expected image cell by cell.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>：快、边缘硬，放大后成块；OpenCV 里叫 INTER_NEAREST。
ops.en: This is <wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>: fast, with hard edges, and blocky when enlarged; OpenCV calls it INTER_NEAREST.

ops.zh: <level-ref to="1D2"></level-ref>里放大成块，但每个旧像素都还在。这一关换一个方向：最近邻缩小图像时，没被选中的旧像素去了哪里？第一个任务把条纹图缩到一半宽、再放大回原宽，同时交出每个新像素的采样位置；第二个任务判断原图的哪些列留在了结果里。
ops.en: In <level-ref to="1D2"></level-ref> enlarging came out blocky, but every old pixel was still there. This level goes the other way: when nearest neighbour shrinks an image, what becomes of the old pixels it does not pick? The first task shrinks striped images to half their width and back again, giving each new pixel's sample position too; the second judges which of the original's columns survive.

ops.zh: <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref>只会照抄：新像素的值只能是原图里已有的某一个，[0, 1] 放大成 3 像素，中间那个不是 0 就是 1。这一关的问题是：新像素落在两个旧像素之间时，它只能等于其中一个吗？
ops.en: The <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref> only copies: a new pixel can take only a value the original already has, so [0, 1] enlarged to 3 pixels has a middle of either 0 or 1. This level asks: when a new pixel falls between two old ones, must it equal one of them?

ops.zh: 测试要的是：[0, 1] 放大成 3 像素时，中间那个是 0.5。这一关的图都只有一行。搭出的元件输入一张图和新的宽、高，交出缩放后的图，测试和隐藏测试的每个值都对才算对。
ops.en: The tests want [0, 1] enlarged to 3 pixels to have 0.5 in the middle. This level's images are all one row high. The part takes an image and a new width and height and gives the resized image, right when every value in the tests and hidden tests is.

ops.zh: 输入一行像素和新的宽、高：交出缩放后的图，每个新像素的值取自它左右两个旧像素。
ops.en: Given a row of pixels and a new width and height, give the resized image, each new pixel's value taken from the two old pixels on its left and right.

value.zh: 中间那个新像素离左右两个旧像素各有多远？
value.en: How far is the middle new pixel from each of the two old ones?

value.zh: 先找出新位置左边那个旧像素，再算新位置离它有多远。
value.en: First find the old pixel to the left of the new position, then how far the position is from it.

value.zh: 两端的新位置落在原图之外：取像素可以设成取最近的边。
value.en: The new positions at the ends fall outside the original: the lookup can be set to read the nearest edge.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：两边按距离加权，权重之和为 1，新值介于两边之间。
ops.en: This is <wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: the two sides weighted by distance, the weights summing to 1, the new value lying between them.

ops.zh: <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>只沿一行插值，竖直方向照抄离得最近的那一行。放大一张二维的图，新像素在上下方向也落在两行之间。这一关的问题是：在二维图像里，落在四个旧像素中间的新像素，值怎么算？
ops.en: The <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref> interpolates only along a row and copies the nearest row vertically. Enlarging a 2D image, a new pixel also falls between two rows. This level asks: in a 2D image, how is the value of a new pixel among four old ones computed?

ops.zh: 两个任务：先用手上的线性缩放只改一张图的宽度，看它在每一行上做了什么；再升级这个元件，让新像素的值由周围四个旧像素决定。升级后的元件要通过二维放大和缩小的测试。
ops.en: Two tasks: first use the linear resizer in hand to change only an image's width and see what it does on each row; then upgrade the part so a new pixel's value comes from the four old pixels around it. The upgraded part must pass tests that enlarge and shrink in two dimensions.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：新值是四个邻居的加权平均，比最近邻平滑；OpenCV 里叫 INTER_LINEAR。
ops.en: This is <wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: the new value a weighted average of four neighbours, smoother than nearest neighbour; OpenCV calls it INTER_LINEAR.

ops.zh: 手上有两种缩放：<part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref>和<part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>。这一关新在取舍：用它们放大同一张图，结果差在哪里？是不是总有一种更好？三个任务：先并排放大，再把结果认到剖面上，最后找出推翻「双线性总比最近邻好」的那组结果。
ops.en: Two resizers are in hand: the <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref> and the <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>. What is new is the trade-off: enlarging one image with each, how do the results differ, and is one always better? Three tasks: enlarge side by side, match the results to profiles, then find the result that refutes 'bilinear is always better than nearest neighbour'.

ops.zh: 电路算出的值是任意的实数，还可能越出 [0, 1]；图像存进文件时，每个值却只能取有限的几级，比如 0 到 255 的整数，共 256 级。工作台还没有办法把一个值存成其中一级。
ops.en: The values a circuit computes are arbitrary real numbers and may leave [0, 1]; stored in a file, though, each value can take only finitely many levels, whole numbers from 0 to 255, say, 256 in all. The workbench has no way yet to store a value as one of them.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：一个值只能存成 L 级中的一级时，该存哪一级？L 级把 [0, 1] 等分，L = 3 时是 0、0.5、1；正好在两级中间时，约定取较大的一级。越出 [0, 1] 的值要先截回来，而加减乘除和向下取整都定不出上下界：新元件<part-ref to="part:min"></part-ref>和<part-ref to="part:max"></part-ref>逐个值取两者中小的、大的。
ops.en: This level asks: when a value can only be stored as one of L levels, which should it be? L levels divide [0, 1] evenly: with L = 3 they are 0, 0.5 and 1; a value exactly between two levels goes to the larger, by convention. Values outside [0, 1] must be brought back first, and neither arithmetic nor floor can set a bound: the new parts <part-ref to="part:min"></part-ref> and <part-ref to="part:max"></part-ref> take the smaller and the larger of two, value by value.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="quantisation"></wiki-ref>：把连续的值存成有限的几级，取最近的一级，不是截掉小数；uint8 就是 256 级。
ops.en: This is <wiki-ref to="quantisation"></wiki-ref>: storing continuous values as finitely many levels, the nearest one, not the fraction cut off; uint8 has 256 levels.

ops.zh: <part-ref to="quantise"></part-ref>把每个值存成最近的一级。这一关新在辨真伪：量化以后，原来的值还能找回来吗？第一个任务让量化器存一张图，同时交出每一格的原值可能落在的范围；第二个任务反过来，从几组输入里选出存成同一个结果的全部输入。
ops.en: The <part-ref to="quantise"></part-ref> stores each value as the nearest level. What is new is testing a belief: after quantisation, can the original values be recovered? The first task has the quantiser store an image and give, for each cell, the range its original may lie in; the second goes backwards and picks, among several inputs, every one stored as the same result.

ops.zh: 流水线常常只要图里的一部分，比如物体所在的那一片。手上的<part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref>改的是整张图的尺寸，每个输出像素都在整张图上采样。这一关的问题是：从一张图里取出一部分时，输出的像素值是原图里已有的，还是新算出来的？
ops.en: A pipeline often wants only part of an image, the region where an object is, say. The <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref> in hand changes the whole image's size, every output pixel sampled across the whole image. This level asks: when part of an image is taken out, are the output's pixel values ones the original holds, or newly computed?

t.zh: 输入一张图、窗口左上角的 x0、y0 和窗口的宽 w、高 h。交出窗口里的像素，测试逐格和原图核对；隐藏测试里有贴边的窗口和彩色图。
t.en: The inputs are an image, the window's top-left x0, y0, and its width w and height h. Give the pixels inside the window; the tests check them cell by cell against the original, and hidden tests include windows on the border and a colour image.

ops.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>：取原数组的子区域，像素值原样保留。<wiki-ref to="numpy"></wiki-ref>写成 image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w]。
ops.en: This is <wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>: a sub-region of the original array, its pixel values kept as they are. In <wiki-ref to="numpy"></wiki-ref> it is image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w].

ops.zh: 识别网络要 S×S 的输入，照片却有各种宽高。手上的缩放元件能把任何图缩成任何尺寸。这一关的问题是：网络要 512×512，手里是 768×512 的照片，直接缩放到 512×512 可以吗？
ops.en: A recognition network wants S×S input, while photos come in every width and height. The resizers in hand can bring any image to any size. This level asks: the network wants 512×512 and the photo is 768×512 — can it be resized straight to 512×512?

ops.zh: 测试图里画着一个正方形的东西：交出的 S×S 图里，它还得是正方形。多出来的部分从两边平均去掉，除不尽时左上少去掉一个像素。横幅和竖幅的照片都要成立。
ops.en: The test images hold something square, and in the S×S result it must still be square. The excess is removed evenly from both sides, one pixel less at the top-left when it does not divide. It must work for landscape and portrait photos alike.

ops.zh: 宽与高之比叫<wiki-ref to="aspect-ratio"></wiki-ref>：宽高各缩各的会改变它，圆变成椭圆；OpenCV 的尺寸写成 (宽, 高)。
ops.en: Width over height is the <wiki-ref to="aspect-ratio"></wiki-ref>: scaling width and height separately changes it and turns circles into ellipses; OpenCV writes a size as (width, height).

ops.zh: 手上已经有<part-ref to="crop"></part-ref>和<part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>。手机的数码变焦没有换镜头，它只有已经拍下的像素。这一关的问题是：它怎样把画面中间放大 k 倍？交出的图和输入一样大，显示原图中心那一部分放大 k 倍后的样子；隐藏测试有非正方形的图和别的 k。
ops.en: The <part-ref to="crop"></part-ref> and the <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref> are in hand. A phone's digital zoom changes no lens; all it has are the pixels already taken. This level asks: how does it magnify the middle of the picture k times? The result is as large as the input and shows the part at the original's centre magnified k times; hidden tests use non-square images and other k.

ops.zh: 数码变焦等于先<wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>、再放大：它只用已有的像素，不带来新的细节；光学变焦换的是镜头的焦距。
ops.en: Digital zoom is <wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref> followed by enlarging: it uses only the pixels already there and adds no detail; optical zoom changes the lens's focal length.

value.zh: 数码变焦只用已有的像素：它放大了画面，没有带来新的细节。
value.en: Digital zoom uses only the pixels already there: it magnifies the picture and brings no new detail.

value.zh: 手机的数码变焦没有换镜头，它手上只有已经拍下的像素。这一关的问题是：它怎样把画面中间放大 k 倍？交出的图和输入一样大，显示的是原图中心那一部分放大 k 倍后的样子。
value.en: A phone's digital zoom changes no lens; all it has are the pixels already taken. This level asks: how does it magnify the middle of the picture k times? The result is as large as the input and shows the part at the original's centre magnified k times.

value.zh: 这样保住了<wiki-ref to="aspect-ratio"></wiki-ref>：宽和高乘同一个比例。
value.en: This keeps the <wiki-ref to="aspect-ratio"></wiki-ref>: width and height scaled by one factor.

value.zh: 测试图里画着一个正方形的东西：交出的 S×S 图里，它还得是正方形，多出来的部分从两边平均去掉，除不尽时左上少去掉一个像素。
value.en: The test images hold something square: in the S×S result it must still be square, and the excess is removed evenly from both sides, one pixel less at the top-left when it does not divide.

value.zh: 识别网络要 S×S 的输入，照片却有各种宽高。这一关的问题是：网络要 512×512，手里是 768×512 的照片，直接缩放到 512×512 可以吗？
value.en: A recognition network wants S×S input, while photos come in every width and height. This level asks: the network wants 512×512 and the photo is 768×512 — can it simply be resized to 512×512?

value.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>：NumPy 写成 image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w]。
value.en: This is <wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>: in NumPy, image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w].

value.zh: 流水线常常只要图里的一部分。这一关的问题是：从一张图里取出一块时，输出的像素值是原图里已有的，还是新算出来的？输入一张图、窗口左上角的 x0、y0 和窗口的宽 w、高 h。
value.en: A pipeline often wants only part of an image. This level asks: when a region is taken out of an image, are the output's pixel values ones the original holds, or newly computed? The inputs are an image, the window's top-left x0, y0, and its width w and height h.

value.zh: 量化器把每个值存成最近的一级。这一关的问题是：量化以后，原来的值还能找回来吗？先让量化器存一张图，同时交出每一格的原值可能落在的范围；再反过来，从几组输入里找出存成同一个结果的那些。
value.en: The quantiser stores each value as the nearest level. This level asks: after quantisation, can the original values be recovered? First have the quantiser store an image and give, for each cell, the range its original value may lie in; then go backwards and find, among several inputs, those stored as one same result.

value.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="quantisation"></wiki-ref>：uint8 就是 256 级的量化。
value.en: This is <wiki-ref to="quantisation"></wiki-ref>: uint8 is quantisation to 256 levels.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：一个值只能存成 L 级中的一级时，该存哪一级？L 级把 [0, 1] 等分，L = 3 时是 0、0.5、1。新元件<part-ref to="part:min"></part-ref>和<part-ref to="part:max"></part-ref>逐个值取两者中小的、大的。正好在两级中间时，约定取较大的一级。
value.en: This level asks: when a value can only be stored as one of L levels, which should it be? L levels divide [0, 1] evenly: with L = 3 they are 0, 0.5 and 1. The new parts <part-ref to="part:min"></part-ref> and <part-ref to="part:max"></part-ref> take the smaller and the larger of two, value by value. A value exactly between two levels goes to the larger, by convention.

value.zh: 图像存进文件时，每个值只能取有限的几级：uint8 有 256 级。电路算出来的值还可能越出 [0, 1]。
value.en: When an image is stored, each value can take only a few levels: uint8 has 256. And values a circuit computes may leave [0, 1].

value.zh: 手上有两种缩放：最近邻和双线性。这一关的问题是：用它们放大同一张图，结果差在哪里？是不是总有一种更好？先并排放大，再把结果认到剖面上，最后判断一句论断。
value.en: Two resizers are in hand: nearest neighbour and bilinear. This level asks: enlarging one image with each, how do the results differ, and is one always better? Enlarge side by side, match the results to profiles, then judge a claim.

value.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：四个权重之和为 1，OpenCV 里叫 INTER_LINEAR。
value.en: This is <wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: four weights summing to 1; OpenCV calls it INTER_LINEAR.

value.zh: 先用手上的线性缩放只改一张图的宽度，看它在每一行上做了什么；再把这块元件升级：新像素由周围四个旧像素加权。
value.en: First use the linear resizer in hand to change only an image's width, and see what it does on each row; then upgrade the part: a new pixel weighted from the four old pixels around it.

value.zh: 线性缩放只沿一行插值，竖直方向照抄离得最近的那一行。这一关的问题是：在二维图像里，落在四个旧像素中间的新像素，值怎么算？
value.en: Linear resizing interpolates only along a row and copies the nearest row vertically. This level asks: in a 2D image, how is the value of a new pixel among four old ones computed?

value.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：权重之和为 1，新值介于两边之间。
value.en: This is <wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: the weights sum to 1 and the new value lies between the two.

value.zh: 先找出新位置左边那个旧像素，再算新位置离它有多远。
value.en: First find the old pixel to the left of the new position, then how far the position is from it.

value.zh: 两端的新位置落在原图之外：取像素可以设成取最近的边。
value.en: The new positions at the ends fall outside the original: the lookup can be set to read the nearest edge.

value.zh: 输入一行像素和新的宽、高：交出缩放后的图，新像素由左右两个旧像素按距离加权。
value.en: Given a row of pixels and a new width and height, give the resized image, each new pixel weighted from its two old neighbours by distance.

value.zh: 测试要的是：[0, 1] 放大成 3 像素时，中间那个是 0.5。新像素的值由它左右两个旧像素决定，离得越近的那个说了算的越多。
value.en: The tests want [0, 1] enlarged to 3 pixels to have 0.5 in the middle. A new pixel's value is decided by the old pixels on its left and right, the nearer one counting for more.

value.zh: 最近邻缩放只会照抄，新像素的值只能是原图里已有的某一个。这一关的问题是：新像素落在两个旧像素之间时，它只能等于其中一个吗？这一关的图都只有一行。
value.en: Nearest-neighbour resizing only copies: a new pixel can only take a value the original already has. This level asks: when a new pixel falls between two old ones, must it equal one of them? This level's images are all one row high.

value.zh: 最近邻缩放放大时成块。这一关换一个方向：最近邻缩小图像时，没被选中的旧像素去了哪里？先把条纹图缩到一半宽、再放大回原来的宽，同时交出每个新像素的采样位置；再判断原图的哪些列留在了结果里。
value.en: Nearest-neighbour enlarging makes squares. This level goes the other way: when nearest neighbour shrinks an image, what becomes of the old pixels it does not pick? First shrink striped images to half their width and enlarge them back, giving each new pixel's sample position as well; then judge which of the original's columns survive.

value.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>：放大后一块一块的，OpenCV 里叫 INTER_NEAREST。
value.en: This is <wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>: enlargements come out in squares; OpenCV calls it INTER_NEAREST.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：放大一张图时，落在两个旧像素之间的新像素，值从哪里来？新元件<part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref>读出图的宽高，<part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref>按整数坐标在图上取值，<part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref>向下取整。离两边一样远时，约定取坐标较大的一边。
value.en: This level asks: when an image is enlarged, where does a new pixel that falls between two old ones get its value? New parts: <part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref> reads an image's width and height, <part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref> reads an image at whole-number coordinates, <part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref> rounds down. When a position is equally far from two pixels, the convention takes the larger coordinate.

value.zh: 有了采样网格，每个新像素都知道自己落在原图的哪里；可这个位置一般不是整数，原图在那里没有像素。
value.en: With the sampling grid every new pixel knows where it sits in the original; but that position is seldom a whole number, and the original has no pixel there.

value.zh: 这就是<wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>：新图的每个像素反向映射回原图。
value.en: This is a <wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>: every pixel of the new image mapped back into the original.

t.zh: 手算一行可以，一整张图就要电路了。新元件：<part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref>（给定宽高，给出每格就是自己 x、y 的两张图），以及<part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref>，它们对数和整张图逐个值地算。
t.en: One row by hand is fine; a whole image needs a circuit. New parts: <part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref>, <part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref> (for a width and height, the two images whose cells hold their own x and y), and <part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>, <part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref> and <part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref>, which work value by value on numbers and whole images.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：图像放大或缩小时，新图的每个像素对应原图的什么位置？约定是新旧两排像素的中心对齐，两排一样长。先在格子上手算一行，再搭一块电路。
value.en: This level asks: when an image is enlarged or shrunk, where in the original does each new pixel sit? The convention: the two rows of pixels are equally long and their centres are aligned. First work out one row by hand on the grid, then wire a circuit.

value.zh: 工作台要能缩放图像。和取出一部分不同，缩放要给新图的每个像素算出一个值；在算值之前，先得知道它落在原图的什么位置。
value.en: The workbench must resize images. Unlike taking out a part, resizing computes a value for every pixel of the new image; before any value, each new pixel needs its position in the original.

value.zh: 像素值有<wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref>和类型：显示时截到两端，存着的数不变。
value.en: Pixel values have a <wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref> and a type: the display clips to the ends, the stored numbers stay.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：两个像素看上去一样白，存着的数一样吗？先填出每格显示出来的值，再把 OpenCV 读进来的 uint8 像素换成 [0, 1] 里的 (R, G, B)。uint8 是 0 到 255 的整数，255 最亮。
value.en: This level asks: when two pixels look equally white, do they hold the same number? First fill in each cell's displayed value, then turn uint8 pixels read by OpenCV into (R, G, B) in [0, 1]. A uint8 is a whole number from 0 to 255, 255 the brightest.

value.zh: 电路算出的值可以落在 [0, 1] 之外。屏幕只显示得出 0 到 1，画的时候超出的部分画成最黑或最白。
value.en: A circuit may compute values outside [0, 1]. A screen shows only 0 to 1, and draws whatever lies beyond as the darkest or the brightest.

value.zh: 各个库的<wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>不同：OpenCV 读图得到 BGR，Matplotlib 按 RGB 显示。
value.en: Libraries differ in <wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>: OpenCV reads images as BGR, Matplotlib displays RGB.

value.zh: 工作台第一次接电路：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。新元件<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出彩色图的一个通道，取哪一个是它的设置：R、G 或 B，也就是每格的第一、第二或第三个数；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图合成一张彩色图。
value.en: The workbench wires its first circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. The new part <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes one channel out of a colour image, and which one is its setting: R, G or B, the first, second or third number of each cell. <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> makes three grey images one colour image.

value.zh: 一张用 OpenCV 读进来的照片，在这里显示出来，蓝天却成了橙色。这一关的问题是：同一张照片，为什么在这里显示出橙色的天空？
value.en: A photo read in with OpenCV is displayed here, and its blue sky has turned orange. This level asks: why does the same photo show an orange sky here?

value.zh: 焦距除以像素尺寸，就是<wiki-ref to="pixel-units"></wiki-ref>。
value.en: The focal length divided by the pixel size is the <wiki-ref to="pixel-units"></wiki-ref>.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：物体在图里高 100 像素，实高 120 mm，离相机 600 mm，镜头的焦距是多少毫米？先算，再到相机台上验证，最后写出以像素计的焦距。
value.en: This level asks: an object is 100 pixels tall in the image, 120 mm tall and 600 mm from the camera — what is the lens's focal length in millimetres? Work it out, check it on the camera bench, then state the focal length in pixels.

value.zh: 图里的长度以像素计，像平面上的长度以毫米计。传感器把两者连起来：它高 20 mm，排着 200 个像素。
value.en: Lengths in the image are counted in pixels, lengths on the image plane in millimetres. The sensor links the two: it is 20 mm tall and holds 200 pixels.

value.zh: 焦距决定看得多宽，这就是<wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>：焦距越短，看得越宽。
value.en: The focal length decides how wide the camera sees: its <wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>. The shorter the focal length, the wider.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：要把一排物体全拍进画面，焦距该变长还是变短？传感器大小不变，物体都在 2000 mm 外，台上只有焦距 f 能动。
value.en: This level asks: to get a whole row of objects into the frame, should the focal length grow or shrink? The sensor stays as it is, the objects stand 2000 mm away, and only the focal length f turns.

value.zh: 像平面不是无限大的：相机台装上一块 20 mm 高、200 像素的传感器，主点在中心。像落到传感器边外的物体，不在画面里。
value.en: The image plane is not endless: the camera bench now holds a sensor 20 mm and 200 pixels tall, its principal point at the centre. An object whose image falls past its edges is out of the picture.

value.zh: 清晰范围在对焦距离的两边都有：只用上一边，另一边就白白浪费了。
value.en: The sharp range extends on both sides of the focus: use only one side and the other is wasted.

value.zh: 两个物体在 1000 mm 和 3000 mm，两个都要清晰，进光量又不能低于 1。这回光圈和对焦距离都能动。这一关的问题是：既要两个深度都清晰，又要足够的光，对焦该放在哪里？
value.en: Two objects stand at 1000 mm and 3000 mm; both must be sharp and the light must not fall below 1. This time the aperture and the focus distance both turn. This level asks: with both depths to keep sharp and enough light to gather, where should the focus go?

value.zh: 同时清晰的深度范围叫<wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>：f 数越大，光圈越小，它越深。
value.en: The range of depths sharp at once is the <wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>: the larger the f-number, the smaller the aperture and the deeper it is.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处两个物体，怎样在一张照片里都清晰？曲线画出每个深度的模糊圈和清晰的门槛；进光量也不能低于 1。
value.en: This level asks: how can a near and a far object both be sharp in one photo? The curve draws each depth's blur circle against the sharpness threshold; and the light must not fall below 1.

value.zh: 透镜对焦在 1500 mm，近处的标记在 1200 mm，远处的在 2000 mm。光圈这回用摄影的写法给出：f 数是焦距除以光圈直径，50 mm 镜头的 f/2 就是 25 mm 的光圈。
value.en: The lens is focused at 1500 mm, with the near marker at 1200 mm and the far one at 2000 mm. The aperture is now given the photographer's way: the f-number is the focal length over the aperture diameter, so f/2 on a 50 mm lens is a 25 mm aperture.

value.zh: <wiki-ref to="lens"></wiki-ref>只把一个距离上的光会聚到一点，别的距离成模糊圈。
value.en: A <wiki-ref to="lens"></wiki-ref> gathers the light of one depth to a point; other depths make blur circles.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：要让图更亮又不变糊，只把孔开大够吗？进光量至少要到 4，近处的箱子还要清晰：它在传感器上的模糊圈不超过 0.03 mm。
value.en: This level asks: to make the image brighter without blurring it, is widening the hole enough? The light must reach at least 4, and the near crate must be sharp: its blur circle on the sensor no wider than 0.03 mm.

value.zh: 针孔小，进来的光少，图很暗；把孔开大，同一点的光会落到传感器上不同的地方。工作台换上一块焦距 50 mm 的透镜：光圈直径 A 管进来多少光，对焦距离管透镜把哪个距离上的光会聚到一点。
value.en: A small pinhole lets in little light and the image is dark; widen it, and light from one point lands at different places on the sensor. The workbench now holds a 50 mm lens: the aperture diameter A sets how much light comes in, the focus distance which depth the lens gathers back to a point.

t.zh: 到这里，任务都是由物体求像。这一关反过来问：看到像有多高，能定出物体有多远吗？焦距固定为 f = 2。每一轮给出几组（物高, 距离），选出像高都是 1、距离又各不相同的那几组，全部选对、一组不多才算对。
t.en: So far every task has gone from the object to its image. This level asks the other way: does the height of an image tell how far away the object is? The focal length is fixed at f = 2. Each round lists several (height, depth) pairs; choose those that all image 1 tall at different depths, all of them and no others.

brief.zh: f = 2：选出像高都是 1、距离各不相同的两组以上。
brief.en: With f = 2, choose two or more pairs that all image 1 tall, each at its own depth.

hint.zh: 物高和距离一起翻倍时，像高怎样变？
hint.en: When height and depth double together, what happens to the image height?

prompt.zh: 哪几组的像高都是 1、距离又各不相同？
prompt.en: Which pairs all image 1 tall at different depths?

prompt.zh: 换一批：哪几组的像高都是 1、距离又各不相同？
prompt.en: A new batch: which pairs all image 1 tall at different depths?

value.zh: 相机台上，同一个像高可以来自不同的物体。焦距 f = 2 固定。这一关的问题是：看到像有多高，能定出物体有多远吗？从几组（物高, 距离）里，选出像高都是 1、距离却各不相同的几组。
value.en: On the camera bench one image height can come from different objects. The focal length is fixed at f = 2. This level asks: does the height of an image tell how far away the object is? From several (height, depth) pairs, choose those that all image 1 tall at different depths.

value.zh: 台上只有像平面的距离 f 能动。先在台上让像高达到目标；再对另外两组数不上台、先算出 f，最后拿其中一组上台验证。
value.en: Only the plane distance f turns on the bench. First bring the image to the target height there; then, for two other sets of numbers, work out f without the bench, and finally check one of them on it.

value.zh: 在针孔相机上，像的大小靠移动物体来改。这一关物体和它的距离都锁住了：物体不动、相机不挪，还有什么能让像变大？
value.en: On the pinhole camera the image size was changed by moving the object. Here the object and its distance are locked: with neither the object nor the camera moving, what else can make the image larger?

value.zh: 这就是<wiki-ref to="pinhole-projection"></wiki-ref>：像的位置和大小都随 f/Z 缩放。
value.en: This is <wiki-ref to="pinhole-projection"></wiki-ref>: where the image lands and how big it is both scale with f/Z.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：一点穿过针孔，落在像平面的什么位置？同一个物体离得越远，像怎样变？每一步只有一个旋钮能动，让像落到圆圈标出的目标上。
value.en: This level asks: where on the image plane does a point land after passing the hole? How does the image change as the object moves away? Each step opens one knob; bring the image onto the circled target.

value.zh: 图里的数从哪里来？工作台先装上相机台：一台理想的针孔相机。场景里一点射出的光穿过针孔，落在离针孔 f 的像平面上。台上把像平面画在针孔前面，像是正的。
value.en: Where do an image's numbers come from? The workbench first gets a camera bench: an ideal pinhole camera. Light from a point of the scene passes through the hole and lands on the image plane at distance f from it. The bench draws the plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright.

value.zh: 这一关从坐标换到数组：按下标点出像素，再从数组的形状读出图的宽和高。库里还有第三种写法：OpenCV 把尺寸写成 (宽, 高)。
value.en: This level moves from coordinates to arrays: pick pixels by index, then read an image's width and height off its array shape. Libraries add a third way of writing it: OpenCV gives a size as (width, height).

value.zh: 程序里读像素用的是数组下标 I[第几行, 第几列]，不是坐标 (x, y)。两种写法说的是同一批像素，顺序却不一样。
value.en: A program reads a pixel by its array index I[row, column], not by coordinates (x, y). The two name the same pixels, in a different order.

value.zh: 这就是<wiki-ref to="pixel-coordinates"></wiki-ref>：原点在左上角，从 0 数起。
value.en: These are <wiki-ref to="pixel-coordinates"></wiki-ref>: the origin at the top-left corner, counting from 0.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：图像坐标 (x, y) 指的是哪一个像素？对着坐标轴点出给定坐标的格子，再反过来写出高亮格子的坐标。
value.en: This level asks: which pixel do image coordinates (x, y) refer to? Reading the axes, pick the cell at given coordinates, then go the other way and write the coordinates of a highlighted cell.

value.zh: 要读写一个像素，先得说清是哪一个。工作台给图上的每一格一对坐标 (x, y)，格子旁边画着两条坐标轴。
value.en: To read or write a pixel one must first say which. The workbench gives every cell of an image a pair of coordinates (x, y), and draws the two axes beside the grid.

value.zh: 灰度图存成 高 × 宽 的<wiki-ref to="image-array"></wiki-ref>，彩色图每格存三个数。
value.en: A grey image is stored as a height × width <wiki-ref to="image-array"></wiki-ref>; a colour image holds three numbers a cell.

value.zh: 彩色图的每个像素存三个数 (R, G, B)：红、绿、蓝各有多亮，各在 0 到 1 之间。
value.en: Each pixel of a colour image stores three numbers (R, G, B): how bright its red, green and blue are, each from 0 to 1.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：相机拍下的这张小图，存进计算机是什么样子？照着画面把每个像素的数填进格子；格子摆成什么形状，图就存成什么形状。
value.en: This level asks: what does this small picture from the camera look like once it is stored in the computer? Following the picture, fill in each pixel's number; the shape of the grid is the shape the image is stored in.

value.zh: 检查台判断得了答案，却碰不到图里的一个数。工作台从这里补起：相机把光变成数，计算机存下的就是这些数。这一章的灰度图里，0 是黑，1 是白，中间的数是不同深浅的灰。
value.en: The station could judge answers but could not touch a single number of an image. The workbench starts here: the camera turns light into numbers, and those numbers are what the computer stores. In this chapter's grey images 0 is black, 1 is white and the numbers between are shades of grey.

why: channel's setting names a position (0, 1, 2), not a colour: the same board, renamed

review [8]: 0B1 teaches one object seen under another viewpoint and light, and rejects a reshaped object; name the point by what it is (appearance variation), not intra-class variation (different instances of one class), which slide 28 does not name and the level marks wrong

value.zh: 外观变化（视角与光照）
value.en: appearance variation (viewpoint and illumination)

value.zh: 同一个物体换了视角或光照，拍出的图几乎每个像素都变了，物体本身却没有变；物体自身的形状变了才是另一个物体。讲义列出的无关变化还有大小和距离、背景、遮挡。识别因此不能记住像素，要找对这些无关变化有容忍度的表示。
value.en: Seen from another viewpoint or under another light, one object yields an image in which nearly every pixel has changed while the object has not; only a change in the object's own shape makes it another object. The lecture's other irrelevant changes are size and distance, background and occlusion. Recognition therefore cannot memorise pixels; it needs a representation tolerant of these irrelevant changes.
