why.en: This map labels each pixel with its class only: every pixel of one class holds the same number, so two touching dogs merge into one region and cannot be counted.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 到这里，请求问的都是类别和位置。一辆车上的视觉系统同时交出五份输出：一个标签、一组检测框和三张逐像素图。车上各个模块的请求由检查台分给它们，其中一个请求问的是距离。
t.en: So far every request has asked about classes and positions. The vision system on a car hands in five outputs at once: a label, a set of detection boxes and three per-pixel maps. The station routes the requests of the car's modules to them, and one request asks about distance.

t.zh: 这一关新在两处：一个请求可以有几份够用的输出，选出够用的都算对；三张图的格子里都是数，含义却不同，而画面不给出，含义只能从图上的数本身判断。这一关的问题是：「那辆车离我多远」该由哪一份回答？类别图里的数能当距离用吗？
t.en: Two things are new here: a request may have several sufficient outputs, and choosing those that suffice is right; and the three maps all hold numbers that mean different things, with no picture shown, so the meaning must come from the numbers themselves. This level asks: which output answers 'how far away is that car'? Can the numbers in a class map serve as distances?

after.zh: 每格是一个距离的图叫<wiki-ref to="depth-map"></wiki-ref>，是三维恢复的输出；类别输出里的数是编号，回答不了「多远」。
after.en: A map whose every cell is a distance is a <wiki-ref to="depth-map"></wiki-ref>, an output of 3D reconstruction; the numbers in a class output are ids and cannot answer 'how far'.

brief.zh: 为每个请求选出能回答它的输出，够用的都可以选。
brief.en: For each request, choose outputs that answer it; any that suffice may be chosen.

hint.zh: 三张图的格子里都是数，有的是编号，有的是类别，有的是长度。比较每张图里各片区域的数。
hint.en: All three maps hold numbers: some are ids, some classes, some lengths. Compare the numbers of the regions within each map.

hint.zh: 两个同类物体在一张图里各有自己的数，还是共用一个？哪张图的数从上往下一路变小，像越来越近的地面？
hint.en: Do two objects of one class get a number each in a map, or share one? In which map do the numbers fall steadily from top to bottom, like ground coming nearer?

prompt.zh: 路面是哪些像素？
prompt.en: Which pixels are road?

prompt.zh: 每个行人各在哪里？
prompt.en: Where is each pedestrian?

prompt.zh: 第 2 行第 4 列那个像素处的车，离相机多远？
prompt.en: How far from the camera is the car at row 2, column 4?

prompt.zh: 最近的那面墙离相机多远？
prompt.en: How far from the camera is the nearest wall?

prompt.zh: 停着几辆车？
prompt.en: How many cars are parked?

prompt.zh: 画面里有行人吗？
prompt.en: Is there a pedestrian in the picture?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 检查台会比较输出和请求了，可识别还要回答「这是不是同一个东西」，而同一个物体换个角度、换盏灯，拍出的像素就全变了。检查台旁边多了一个受控的小场景：一个物体、一架能绕着它转的相机和一盏灯。场景渲出的图，可以拿来和候选图比较。
t.en: The station can now compare outputs with requests, but recognition must also say whether two pictures show the same thing, and one object seen from another angle or under another lamp gives entirely different pixels. Beside the station there is now a small controlled scene: one object, a camera that orbits it and a lamp. What the scene renders can be compared with the candidates.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：两张图的像素几乎都不同，拍的会是同一个物体吗？参照图拍的是场景里的那个物体。第一个任务只能转相机，第二个任务只能移灯；每一轮选出拍的也是它的全部候选图，一张不多，一张不少。
t.en: This level asks: when two pictures differ in almost every pixel, can they show the same object? The reference shows the object in the scene. In the first task only the camera turns, in the second only the lamp moves; in each round choose every candidate that shows that object too, no more and no fewer.

after.zh: 同一个物体换视角、换光照，像素几乎全变，这是<wiki-ref to="intra-class-variation"></wiki-ref>：识别要容忍它，不能靠记住像素。
after.en: One object under another viewpoint or light changes nearly every pixel: this is <wiki-ref to="intra-class-variation"></wiki-ref>, which recognition must tolerate instead of memorising pixels.

brief.zh: 转动场景的相机，选出拍的是参照图里那个物体的全部候选图。
brief.en: Turn the scene's camera, and choose every candidate that shows the object of the reference.

hint.zh: 别逐个比像素：转动相机，看场景能不能渲出和候选图一样的画面。
hint.en: Do not compare pixels one by one: turn the camera and see whether the scene can render the candidate's picture.

after.zh: 换了视角的图和参照图几乎没有一个像素相同，物体却没变。接下来动的是灯。
after.en: Pictures from another viewpoint share almost no pixel with the reference, yet the object is the same. Now the lamp moves.

prompt.zh: 哪几张图拍的是参照图里的物体？
prompt.en: Which pictures show the object of the reference?

prompt.zh: 这一组里，哪几张图拍的是参照图里的物体？
prompt.en: In this set, which pictures show the object of the reference?

why.zh: 这张和参照图视角相同，像素最像，可物体的形状变了；转过视角的那几张像素几乎全不同，转动相机却渲得出来。
why.en: This picture shares the reference's view and most of its pixels, yet the object's shape has changed; the turned pictures differ in nearly every pixel, and turning the camera renders them.

brief.zh: 调动场景的灯，选出拍的是参照图里那个物体的全部候选图。
brief.en: Move the scene's lamp, and choose every candidate that shows the object of the reference.

hint.zh: 相机这次不动：明暗和影子变了，物体的形状变没变？
hint.en: The camera stays put this time: the shading and the shadows changed, but did the object's shape?

prompt.zh: 哪几张图拍的是参照图里的物体？
prompt.en: Which pictures show the object of the reference?

why.zh: 这张的明暗和参照图一样，靠背却换了地方；光照变了的那几张，调灯就渲得出来。
why.en: This picture's shading matches the reference, but the chair back has moved; the relit pictures are what the lamp renders when moved.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 检查台看出了同一个物体能拍成很不一样的图。一个分类器面对这些变化能不能照样认对，要靠检验。它的作者说：「它在任何背景下都认得出猫。」检查台拿到几批样例，每个样例写着人工标注的类别、背景、分类器的预测和置信度。
t.en: The station has seen that one object can be photographed very differently. Whether a classifier still answers right through such changes has to be tested. Its author claims: 'it recognises a cat against any background.' The station receives a few batches of cases, each listing the labelled class, the background, the classifier's prediction and its confidence.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：分类器在一张照片上答对了，而且很有把握，这能说明它换了背景也认得出吗？每一批选出一个能推翻这句话的样例；一个也没有时，选「没有」。
t.en: This level asks: when a classifier gets one photo right, and confidently, does that show it will recognise the cat against other backgrounds? In each batch choose a case that refutes the claim; when there is none, choose 'none'.

after.zh: 无关变化下输出仍可靠，叫<wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>：一个反例就能推翻它；只改几个像素的<wiki-ref to="adversarial-example"></wiki-ref>也是反例。
after.en: An output that stays reliable through irrelevant change shows <wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>; one counterexample refutes it, and an <wiki-ref to="adversarial-example"></wiki-ref>, a few pixels changed, is one too.

brief.zh: 选出能推翻「它在任何背景下都认得出猫」的样例；没有就选「没有」。
brief.en: Choose a case that refutes 'it recognises a cat against any background'; if there is none, choose 'none'.

hint.zh: 置信度说的是分类器自己有多肯定，不是它对不对：逐个把预测和标注对一对。
hint.en: The confidence says how sure the classifier is, not whether it is right: check each prediction against its label.

prompt.zh: 哪个样例推翻了这句话？
prompt.en: Which case refutes the claim?

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：沙发 · 预测：猫（99%）
label.en: label: cat · background: sofa · predicted: cat (99%)

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：草地 · 预测：猫（92%）
label.en: label: cat · background: grass · predicted: cat (92%)

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：雪地 · 预测：狐狸（71%）
label.en: label: cat · background: snow · predicted: fox (71%)

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：窗台 · 预测：猫（88%）
label.en: label: cat · background: windowsill · predicted: cat (88%)

prompt.zh: 这一批里，哪个样例推翻了这句话？
prompt.en: In this batch, which case refutes the claim?

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：地毯 · 预测：猫（64%）
label.en: label: cat · background: carpet · predicted: cat (64%)

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：车顶 · 预测：猫（97%）
label.en: label: cat · background: car roof · predicted: cat (97%)

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：书架 · 预测：猫（58%）
label.en: label: cat · background: bookshelf · predicted: cat (58%)

prompt.zh: 又一批样例：哪个推翻了这句话？
prompt.en: Another batch: which case refutes the claim?

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：沙滩 · 预测：狗（98%）
label.en: label: cat · background: beach · predicted: dog (98%)

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：厨房 · 预测：猫（81%）
label.en: label: cat · background: kitchen · predicted: cat (81%)

label.zh: 标注：猫 · 背景：树枝 · 预测：猫头鹰（55%）
label.en: label: cat · background: branch · predicted: owl (55%)

why.zh: 这个样例的预测和标注一致：答对的样例，置信度再高，也推翻不了「任何背景下都认得出」。要找的是预测和标注不一致的那个。
why.en: This case's prediction matches its label: a right answer, however confident, cannot refute 'recognises it against any background'. Look for a case whose prediction differs from its label.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 在<level-ref to="0B2"></level-ref>里，检查台检验的是别人的论断，样例是现成的。这一关方向反过来：由检查台替一个杯子分类器设计检验，从一批拍杯子的样例里挑出一组测试集。
t.en: In <level-ref to="0B2"></level-ref> the station judged someone else's claim against cases already given. This level turns the other way: the station designs the test for a mug classifier, picking a test set out of a batch of photos of a mug.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：要检验它的<wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>，测试集里该放哪些样例？看每张样例和一张普通的正面照比变了什么：视角、光照，还是有东西挡在杯子前面。选出的一组要把这三种变化都覆盖到。
t.en: This level asks: to test its <wiki-ref to="robustness"></wiki-ref>, which cases belong in the test set? See what each case changes against a plain front view: the viewpoint, the light, or something standing in front of the mug. The set you choose must cover all three changes.

brief.zh: 选出一组样例，让它覆盖换视角、换光照和有东西挡在前面三种变化。
brief.en: Choose a set of cases that covers a changed viewpoint, changed lighting and something standing in front.

hint.zh: 几张几乎一样的照片只算检验了一种情况；一张照片也可能同时变了两样。
hint.en: Several near-identical photos test only one situation; one photo may change two things at once.

prompt.zh: 选出测试集
prompt.en: Choose the test set

prompt.zh: 换一批样例，再选出测试集
prompt.en: A new batch: choose the test set again

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 到这里，检查台默认答案就在图里。可图是由场景生成的：<wiki-ref to="computer-graphics"></wiki-ref>从物体、材质、光照和相机出发，正向渲出图像；视觉走反方向，手里只有图，要说出场景是什么样。
t.en: So far the station has assumed the answer is in the image. But images are generated from scenes: <wiki-ref to="computer-graphics"></wiki-ref> renders an image forwards from objects, materials, light and a camera; vision goes the other way, holding only the image and having to say what the scene is like.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：只看这一张图，箱子离相机多远？题目给出这张图和几个都渲得出它的候选场景，判断关于场景的每句话：在每个候选场景里都对，才算成立；都错是不成立；有对有错就是无法确定。
t.en: This level asks: from this image alone, how far is the box from the camera? You get the image and several candidate scenes that all render it, and judge each statement about the scene: true in every candidate, it holds; false in every one, it does not; true in some and false in others, it is undetermined.

after.zh: 从图像推回场景是<wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>：三维投成二维丢了一维，不同的场景能渲出同一张图。
after.en: Inferring the scene from the image is an <wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>: projecting 3D to 2D loses a dimension, and different scenes can render the same image.

brief.zh: 判断关于场景的每句话：成立、不成立，还是无法确定。
brief.en: Judge each statement about the scene: holds, does not hold, or undetermined.

hint.zh: 箱子在图里的大小，取决于它有多大，也取决于它有多远。
hint.en: How big the box looks in the image depends on how big it is, and also on how far away.

prompt.zh: 红色箱子离相机 2 米。
prompt.en: The red box is 2 m from the camera.

prompt.zh: 箱子是红色的。
prompt.en: The box is red.

prompt.zh: 箱子高 0.5 米。
prompt.en: The box is 0.5 m tall.

prompt.zh: 箱子是蓝色的。
prompt.en: The box is blue.

prompt.zh: 右边的立方体离相机 2 米。
prompt.en: The cube on the right is 2 m from the camera.

prompt.zh: 左边的立方体是红色的。
prompt.en: The cube on the left is red.

prompt.zh: 右边的立方体在画面里看得见。
prompt.en: The cube on the right shows in the picture.

prompt.zh: 左边的立方体高 0.4 米。
prompt.en: The cube on the left is 0.4 m tall.

why.zh: 按箱子在图里的大小定出了一个距离：可小而近的箱子和大而远的箱子渲出同一张图，距离和高度在候选场景里各不相同。
why.en: That reads one distance off the box's size in the image, but a small near box and a large far one render the same picture: depth and height differ between the candidate scenes.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 在<level-ref to="0C1"></level-ref>里，图上看得见的东西也可能有几种解释。这一关场景里立着一块不透明的挡板，挡住了它后面的东西：被<wiki-ref to="occlusion"></wiki-ref>的部分，图里一个像素也没有。题目照样给出一张图和几个都渲得出它的候选场景。
t.en: In <level-ref to="0C1"></level-ref> even what the image shows allowed several explanations. Here an opaque screen stands in the scene and hides what is behind it: a part lost to <wiki-ref to="occlusion"></wiki-ref> has not one pixel in the image. As before you get the image and several candidate scenes that all render it.

t.zh: 这一关新在看不见的东西：图里看不到的，图像能说明它是什么吗？关于看得见的物体和关于挡板后面的话，都按候选场景判断，每个场景里都对才算成立，每个场景里都错才算不成立。
t.en: What is new is the unseen: can an image say what something it does not show is? Statements about the visible objects and about what is behind the screen are judged alike against the candidate scenes: true in every one, they hold; false in every one, they do not.

brief.zh: 挡板挡住了场景的一部分：判断每句话成立、不成立，还是无法确定。
brief.en: A screen hides part of the scene: judge whether each statement holds, does not hold, or is undetermined.

hint.zh: 露出来的一角只说明那里有东西、是什么颜色；它后面还连着什么，图里没有。
hint.en: A corner showing says only that something is there and what colour it is; what it is attached to behind the screen is not in the image.

hint.zh: 一个东西整个藏在挡板后面时，图里连「没有它」也看不出来。
hint.en: When something hides entirely behind the screen, the image cannot even show that it is absent.

prompt.zh: 挡板右边露出一角的东西是一辆车。
prompt.en: The thing whose corner shows at the screen's right is a car.

prompt.zh: 露出一角的东西是蓝色的。
prompt.en: The thing whose corner shows is blue.

prompt.zh: 场景里没有球。
prompt.en: There is no ball in the scene.

prompt.zh: 挡板是红色的。
prompt.en: The screen is red.

prompt.zh: 挡板后面有一只狗。
prompt.en: There is a dog behind the screen.

prompt.zh: 最左边的箱子在画面里看得见。
prompt.en: The crate at the far left shows in the picture.

prompt.zh: 场景里没有猫。
prompt.en: There is no cat in the scene.

prompt.zh: 最左边的箱子是绿色的。
prompt.en: The crate at the far left is green.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth
A task for a rescue robot

t.zh: 检查台会判断一份输出够不够回答请求，会找反例，也知道一张图说明不了什么。这一关把三样放进一个应用：一台救援机器人在倒塌的楼里找人，找到一个就要靠过去。它的视觉系统交出什么、怎样检验、哪些问题单凭一张图答不了，都由检查台来定。
t.en: The station can judge whether an output answers a request, find counterexamples, and tell what one image cannot settle. This level puts the three into one application: a rescue robot searches a collapsed building and must go to each person it finds. What its vision system hands in, how that is tested and which questions one image cannot answer are all for the station to decide.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：机器人要找到每个人并靠过去，它的视觉输出要包含什么，又该怎样检验？三个任务依次是：为请求选输出，为每种预测配上检验它的参照，再判断几句关于现场的话。新的一点是：输出要包含什么，由机器人接下来要做的动作决定。
t.en: This level asks: a rescue robot must find every person and go to them — what must its vision output contain, and how should it be tested? The three tasks: choose outputs for the requests, pair each kind of prediction with a reference that tests it, then judge a few statements about the site. What is new: the robot's next action decides what the output must contain.

brief.zh: 为机器人的每个请求选出刚好够用的输出。
brief.en: For each of the robot's requests, choose the output that is just enough.

hint.zh: 机器人要靠过去：它得知道往哪里走。
hint.en: The robot must go to the person: it needs to know where to head.

after.zh: 输出选定了。接下来要定怎样检验它。
after.en: The outputs are chosen. Next, how to test them.

prompt.zh: 找出每个人，好一个一个靠过去。
prompt.en: Find every person, so as to go to each in turn.

prompt.zh: 这一层还有没有人？
prompt.en: Is anyone left on this floor?

label.en: a distance in metres at every pixel

prompt.zh: 在这个房间里搜寻机器人要去救的人。
prompt.en: Search this room for the people the robot must reach.

prompt.zh: 门洞离机器人多远？
prompt.en: How far is the doorway from the robot?

label.zh: 一张 48 × 36 的距离网格（米）
label.en: a 48 × 36 grid of distances in metres

brief.zh: 为每一种预测选出能拿来检验它的参照。
brief.en: For each kind of prediction, choose the reference it can be tested against.

hint.zh: 预测和参照要量同一种东西，才比得出对错。
hint.en: A prediction and its reference must measure the same kind of thing for one to check the other.

after.zh: 每种预测都有了检验它的参照。最后看一张图本身能说明多少。
after.en: Every prediction has a reference to test it. Last, how much one image can tell.

prompt.en: Predicted: person (6, 4)–(12, 20)

prompt.zh: 预测：最近的人 3.1 米
prompt.en: Predicted: nearest person 3.1 m

prompt.zh: 预测：画面里有人
prompt.en: Predicted: a person is in view

label.zh: 卷尺：这个人身高 1.7 米
label.en: tape measure: this person stands 1.7 m tall

label.zh: 人工标注：画面里 2 个人
激光测距：到最近的人 3.4 米
label.en: laser range finder: 3.4 m to the nearest person

prompt.zh: 预测：门口的人 7.4 米
prompt.en: Predicted: the person by the door 7.4 m
Predicted: person (30, 10)–(36, 22)

label.en: tape measure: the door is 0.9 m wide

label.zh: 卷尺：沿地面从机器人量到那个人，7.0 米
label.en: tape measure: 7.0 m along the floor from the robot to that person

why.zh: 这是按单位配的：米配米、像素坐标配像素坐标。身高不是距离，一个点不是一个框，人数也不是类别：参照和预测量的是同一种东西，才检验得了它。
why.en: That pairs by unit: metres with metres, pixel coordinates with pixel coordinates. A height is not a distance, one point is not a box, and a head count is not a class: a reference tests a prediction only when both measure the same thing.

brief.zh: 对着机器人拍下的图和候选场景，判断每句话成立、不成立，还是无法确定。
brief.en: Given the robot's picture and the candidate scenes, judge whether each statement holds, does not hold, or is undetermined.

hint.zh: 每个候选场景都渲得出机器人拍到的这张图。
hint.en: Every candidate scene renders the very picture the robot took.

prompt.zh: 左边那个人离机器人 3 米。
prompt.en: The person on the left is 3 m from the robot.

prompt.zh: 场景里正好有两个人。
prompt.en: There are exactly two people in the scene.

prompt.zh: 场景里有一只狗。
prompt.en: There is a dog in the scene.

prompt.zh: 右边那个人是紫色的。
prompt.en: The person on the right is purple.

prompt.zh: 左边那个人在画面里看得见。
prompt.en: The person on the left shows in the picture.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 检查台能判断答案，却说不出图里的数从哪里来，也读不了、改不了、算不了一个像素。这一章给它装上相机与图像工作台：先弄清一张图怎样存成数，再搭相机模型和处理图像的电路。
t.en: The station could judge answers but could not say where an image's numbers come from, nor read, change or compute a single pixel. This chapter gives it a camera and image workbench: first how an image is stored as numbers, then camera models and circuits that process images.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：相机拍下的这张小图，存进计算机是什么样子？画面旁边是一张空格子，行数和列数由你填出的样子决定。灰度图里每个<wiki-ref to="pixel"></wiki-ref>是一个数：0 是黑，1 是白，中间是不同深浅的灰。照着画面填，形状和每个数都对才算对。
t.en: This level asks: what does this small picture from the camera look like once it is stored in the computer? Beside the picture is an empty grid whose rows and columns are whatever you fill in. In a grey image each <wiki-ref to="pixel"></wiki-ref> is one number: 0 is black, 1 is white, and the numbers between are shades of grey. Fill it from the picture; it is right when the shape and every number are.

after.zh: 灰度图存成 高 × 宽 的<wiki-ref to="image-array"></wiki-ref>，彩色图再多一维通道：高 × 宽 × 3。像素只说多亮，不说多远。
after.en: A grey image is stored as a height × width <wiki-ref to="image-array"></wiki-ref>, a colour image with one more axis for channels: height × width × 3. A pixel says how bright, not how far.

brief.zh: 照着画面，把这张 3 像素宽、2 像素高的灰度图存成一格格的数。
brief.en: Following the picture, store this grey image, 3 pixels wide and 2 high, as cells of numbers.

hint.zh: 画面里只有三种颜色：黑、中灰、白。
hint.en: The picture holds only three shades: black, mid grey and white.

why.zh: 这是按 宽 × 高 抄的：画面的第一行像素抄成了格子的第一列。数组先写高、再写宽，格子的第 y 行就是画面的第 y 行。
why.en: This is copied as width × height: the picture's first row went into the grid's first column. An array lists height first, then width; row y of the grid is row y of the picture.

brief.zh: 再存一张 2 像素宽、3 像素高的灰度图。
brief.en: Now store a grey image 2 pixels wide and 3 high.

hint.zh: 画面里的一行像素，存成格子里的哪一行？
hint.en: Which row of the grid does a row of pixels in the picture go to?

why.zh: 这张图 2 像素宽、3 像素高，抄出来却是 2 行 3 列：行和列对调了，每一行要是画面里的一行像素。
why.en: The image is 2 pixels wide and 3 high, but this copy has 2 rows of 3: rows and columns are swapped, and each row must be one row of the picture's pixels.

t.zh: 彩色图多一维<wiki-ref to="channel"></wiki-ref>：每个像素存三个数 (R, G, B)，说红、绿、蓝各有多亮，各在 0 到 1 之间。
t.en: A colour image has one more axis, the <wiki-ref to="channel"></wiki-ref>: each pixel stores three numbers (R, G, B), how bright its red, green and blue are, each from 0 to 1.

brief.zh: 把第二行正中间那个像素改成纯蓝，别的格子不动。
brief.en: Turn the middle pixel of the second row pure blue, leaving every other cell as it is.

hint.zh: 纯蓝：蓝色最亮，红和绿一点也没有。
hint.en: Pure blue: the blue at its brightest, no red and no green at all.

why.zh: 只把第二行正中间那个像素的蓝色调到 1，得到 (1, 1, 1)，那是白色：纯蓝还要红和绿都是 0。
why.en: Raising only the blue number of the middle pixel in the second row gives (1, 1, 1), which is white: pure blue also needs its red and green at 0.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 数存好了，要读写其中一个像素，先得说清是哪一个。工作台给图上的每一格一对坐标 (x, y)，格子旁边画着两条坐标轴。
t.en: The numbers are stored; to read or write one pixel, one must first say which. The workbench gives every cell of an image a pair of coordinates (x, y) and draws the two axes beside the grid.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：图像坐标 (x, y) 指的是哪一个像素？前两个任务对着坐标轴点出给定坐标的格子，其中一张图宽高不等；第三个任务反过来，写出高亮格子的坐标。点中或写对那一格才算对。
t.en: This level asks: which pixel do image coordinates (x, y) refer to? The first two tasks have you pick the cell at given coordinates by the axes, one of them on an image whose width and height differ; the third goes the other way and asks for the coordinates of a highlighted cell. Only the right cell counts.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="pixel-coordinates"></wiki-ref>：原点在左上角，从 0 数起，y 向下增大，和数学课上 y 轴朝上的坐标不同。
after.en: These are <wiki-ref to="pixel-coordinates"></wiki-ref>: the origin at the top-left corner, counting from 0, y growing downwards, unlike the upward y of school geometry.

brief.zh: 点出坐标 (0, 1) 的像素。
brief.en: Pick the pixel at coordinates (0, 1).

hint.zh: 先看坐标轴上 0 在哪个角，y 往哪个方向增大。
hint.en: First see which corner the axes start at, and which way y grows.

why.zh: 这是像数学课那样让 y 从最下面一行往上数：图像坐标的 y 从最上面一行往下数，(0, 1) 是左上角往下一格。
why.en: That counts y upwards from the bottom row, as in school geometry: image y counts down from the top row, so (0, 1) is one cell below the top-left corner.

brief.zh: 在这张宽高不等的图上点出 (2, 0)。
brief.en: On this image, whose width and height differ, pick (2, 0).

why.zh: y = 0 被当成了最下面一行：图像的第 0 行在最上面，(2, 0) 在右上角。
why.en: y = 0 was taken as the bottom row: an image's row 0 is at the top, so (2, 0) is the top-right cell.

brief.zh: 写出高亮像素的坐标 (x, y)。
brief.en: Write the coordinates (x, y) of the highlighted pixel.

hint.zh: x 数的是第几列，y 数的是第几行。
hint.en: x counts the column, y the row.

why.zh: x 和 y 写反了：这张图只有 3 列，x = 3 已经在图外；x 数列，y 数行。
why.en: x and y are swapped: this image has only 3 columns, so x = 3 lies outside it; x counts columns, y rows.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: <level-ref to="1A2"></level-ref>用的是坐标 (x, y)，程序里读像素用的却是数组下标 I[第几行, 第几列]。两种写法说的是同一批像素，顺序不一样。
t.en: <level-ref to="1A2"></level-ref> used coordinates (x, y), but a program reads a pixel by its array index I[row, column]. The two name the same pixels in a different order.

t.zh: 这一关新在方向：从坐标换到数组。先按下标点出像素；再只凭数组的形状说出图的宽和高，图本身不给；最后把<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>报出的尺寸换成数组形状。每一问都要点中那一格或选对那一对数。
t.en: What is new is the direction: from coordinates to arrays. Pick a pixel by its index; then say an image's width and height from its array shape alone, with no image to count; last, turn a size reported by <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref> into an array shape. Each task wants the right cell or the right pair of numbers.

brief.zh: 点出数组元素 I[1, 2] 所在的像素。
brief.en: Pick the pixel that holds the array element I[1, 2].

hint.zh: 这张图只有 2 行。
hint.en: This image has only 2 rows.

why.zh: 把 I[1, 2] 当成了坐标 (x, y) = (1, 2)：这张图只有第 0、1 两行，y = 2 出了界。数组的第一个下标是行，也就是 y。
why.en: That reads I[1, 2] as the coordinates (x, y) = (1, 2): this image has only rows 0 and 1, so y = 2 is outside it. The array's first index is the row, that is y.

brief.zh: 只给出数组的形状：选出这张图的宽和高。
brief.en: Only the array shape is given: choose the image's width and height.

hint.zh: 形状的每一维数的是什么：行，还是列？
hint.en: What does each entry of the shape count: rows, or columns?

prompt.zh: 一张灰度图，数组形状是 (2, 3)。
prompt.en: A grey image whose array shape is (2, 3).

prompt.zh: 一张灰度图，数组形状是 (480, 640)。
prompt.en: A grey image whose array shape is (480, 640).

why.zh: 把形状当成了 (宽, 高)：形状先数行，(2, 3) 是 2 行、每行 3 个像素，也就是高 2、宽 3。
why.en: That reads the shape as (width, height). A shape counts the rows first: (2, 3) is 2 rows of 3 pixels, so 2 tall and 3 wide.

brief.zh: 由 OpenCV 报出的尺寸，选出图的数组形状。
brief.en: From the size OpenCV reports, choose the image's array shape.

hint.zh: 第一轮里那张已知宽高的照片，OpenCV 先报的是哪一个数？
hint.en: For the photo in the first round whose width and height are known, which number does OpenCV report first?

prompt.zh: 一张宽 640、高 480 的照片，OpenCV 报出的尺寸是 (640, 480)。另一张灰度图，OpenCV 报出 (300, 200)：它的数组形状是？
prompt.en: For a photo 640 wide and 480 tall, OpenCV reports the size (640, 480). For another grey image it reports (300, 200): what is that image's array shape?

prompt.zh: 用 OpenCV 把一张灰度图缩放到尺寸 (64, 32)：得到的数组形状是？
prompt.en: OpenCV resizes a grey image to the size (64, 32): what is the resulting array's shape?

why.zh: 把 OpenCV 的尺寸原样抄成了形状：OpenCV 的尺寸先写宽，是 (宽, 高)；数组形状先写行数，是 (高, 宽)，两者正好反过来。
why.en: That copies OpenCV's size straight into the shape. OpenCV's size puts the width first, (width, height); an array shape puts the rows first, (height, width): the one is the other reversed.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 工作台能存、能读像素，却说不出这些数从哪里来：场景里的一点，落到图上的哪个位置？相机台从一台理想的针孔相机起步：一点射出的光穿过针孔，落在离针孔 f 的<wiki-ref to="image-plane"></wiki-ref>上，f 叫<wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref>。台上把像平面画在针孔前面，像是正的。
t.en: The workbench can store and read pixels but cannot say where the numbers come from: where in the image does a point of the scene land? The camera bench starts with an ideal pinhole camera: light from a point passes the hole and lands on the <wiki-ref to="image-plane"></wiki-ref> at distance f from it, f being the <wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref>. The bench draws the plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：一点穿过针孔，落在像平面的什么位置？同一个物体离得越远，像怎样变？两个任务各只开一个旋钮：先横向移动一点，再前后移动一支箭。先想好放在哪里再按「检查」，检查之后才画出光线和像；像落到圆圈标出的目标上才算对。
t.en: This level asks: where on the image plane does a point land after passing the hole, and how does the image change as the object moves away? Each of the two tasks opens one knob: first move a point sideways, then move an arrow in depth. Decide where to put it before you press Check; the rays and the image are drawn only once you check. It is right when the image lands on the circled target.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="pinhole-projection"></wiki-ref>：像的位置和大小按 f/Z 缩放；讲义把像平面画在针孔前面，只是坐标约定。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="pinhole-projection"></wiki-ref>: where the image lands and how big it is scale with f/Z; drawing the plane in front of the hole is only a coordinate convention.

brief.zh: f = 2、Z = 4：横向移动这一点，让它的像落在 u = 1 的标记上。
brief.en: With f = 2 and Z = 4, move the point sideways so its image lands on the mark at u = 1.

hint.zh: 顺着画出的光线看：它从物体出发，穿过针孔，停在像平面上。
hint.en: Follow the drawn ray: it leaves the object, passes the hole and stops on the image plane.

why.zh: 把物体放在 X = 1，像却只落到 u = 0.5：像不在物体的高度上，它按 f/Z 缩小了。
why.en: With the point at X = 1 its image lands only at u = 0.5: the image is not at the object's height, it is shrunk by f/Z.

brief.zh: 箭高 2、f = 2：只前后移动这支箭，让像高等于 0.5。
brief.en: An arrow 2 tall, f = 2: move the arrow only in depth so its image is 0.5 tall.

hint.zh: 检查一次 Z = 2，看像有多高；距离加倍，像高会怎样？
hint.en: Check once at Z = 2 and see how tall the image is; what happens to it when the depth doubles?

why.zh: 以为距离每加 1，像高就少同样一截：像高按 1/Z 变化，Z = 5 时是 0.8。
why.en: Assuming each unit of depth takes the same amount off the image: the height goes as 1/Z, and at Z = 5 it is 0.8.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 在<level-ref to="1B1"></level-ref>里，像的大小靠移动物体来改。这一关物体和它的距离都锁住了：物体不动、相机不挪，还有什么能让像变大？
t.en: In <level-ref to="1B1"></level-ref> the image size changed when the object moved. Here the object and its distance are locked: with neither the object nor the camera moving, what else can make the image larger?

t.zh: 这一关新在改相机，不改场景：台上只有<wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref> f 能动。先在台上让像高达到目标；再不上台，为另外两组数算出 f；最后拿其中一组上台验证，像高等于目标才算对。
t.en: What is new is changing the camera instead of the scene: only the <wiki-ref to="focal-length"></wiki-ref> f turns. First bring the image to the target height on the bench; then work out f for two other sets of numbers without it; finally check one of them on the bench, where the image must match the target.

brief.zh: 物高 1、距离 4 都固定：只调像平面距离 f，让像高等于 1。
brief.en: Object height 1 and depth 4 are fixed: adjust only the plane distance f so the image is 1 tall.

hint.zh: 检查一次 f = 1 时的像高，再想 f 要变成几倍。
hint.en: Check the image height once at f = 1, then work out how many times longer f must be.

why.zh: 以为像平面挪近，像会变大：f 越短，光线越早落到像平面上，像越小。
why.en: Assuming a nearer plane gives a larger image: the shorter f, the sooner the rays meet the plane and the smaller the image.

brief.zh: 不上台，先算：每组数要把像平面放在多远？
brief.en: Without the bench, work it out: how far must the plane stand for each set?

hint.zh: 像高、物高、距离和 f 之间的比例，在台上已经看到过。
hint.en: The bench has already shown how image height, object height, depth and f relate.

prompt.zh: 物高 1.5、距离 6，要像高 1：f 是多少？
prompt.en: Height 1.5, depth 6, image height wanted 1: what is f?

prompt.zh: 物高 2、距离 10，要像高 0.5：f 是多少？
prompt.en: Height 2, depth 10, image height wanted 0.5: what is f?

brief.zh: 物高 2、距离 10：把 f 设成你算出的值，看像高是不是 0.5。
brief.en: Height 2, depth 10: set f to the value you worked out, and see whether the image is 0.5 tall.

why.zh: f = 像高 × 距离，漏掉了物高：物高是 2，f = 5 时像高是 1，是目标的两倍。
why.en: f = image height × depth leaves out the object's height: with H = 2, f = 5 gives an image 1 tall, twice the target.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 到这里，任务都是由物体求像。这一关反过来问：看到像有多高，能定出物体有多远吗？焦距固定为 f = 2。每一轮给出几组（物高, 距离），选出至少两组：选中的每一组像高都是 1，各组的距离互不相同。
t.en: So far every task has gone from the object to its image. This level asks the other way: does the height of an image tell how far away the object is? The focal length is fixed at f = 2. Each round lists several (height, depth) pairs; choose at least two, every one of them imaging 1 tall and no two at the same depth.

after.zh: 像只定出物高和距离的比 H/Z：大而远和小而近成同一个像，这是<wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>在相机上的样子。
after.en: An image fixes only the ratio H/Z: large-and-far and small-and-near image alike — the <wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref> as the camera poses it.

brief.zh: f = 2：选出像高都是 1、距离各不相同的两组以上。
brief.en: With f = 2, choose two or more pairs that all image 1 tall, each at its own depth.

hint.zh: 物高和距离一起翻倍时，像高怎样变？
hint.en: When height and depth double together, what happens to the image height?

prompt.zh: 哪几组的像高都是 1、距离又各不相同？
prompt.en: Which pairs all image 1 tall at different depths?

prompt.zh: 换一批：哪几组的像高都是 1、距离又各不相同？
prompt.en: A new batch: which pairs all image 1 tall at different depths?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 针孔小，进来的光少，图很暗；把孔开大，同一点的光会落到传感器上不同的地方，图就糊。相机台在针孔的位置换上一块焦距 50 mm 的透镜，开两个旋钮：<wiki-ref to="aperture"></wiki-ref>直径 A 管进来多少光，对焦距离是透镜对准的那个距离。
t.en: A small pinhole lets in little light and the image is dark; widen it and light from one point lands at different places on the sensor, and the image blurs. The camera bench puts a 50 mm lens where the hole was and opens two knobs: the <wiki-ref to="aperture"></wiki-ref> diameter A sets how much light comes in, and the focus distance is the distance the lens is set to.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：要让图更亮又不变糊，只把孔开大够吗？台上有近处的箱子和远处的树。进光量至少要到 4，近处的箱子还要清晰：它在传感器上的<wiki-ref to="blur-circle"></wiki-ref>不超过 0.03 mm。
t.en: This level asks: to make the image brighter without blurring it, is widening the hole enough? The bench holds a near crate and a far tree. The light must reach at least 4, and the near crate must be sharp: its <wiki-ref to="blur-circle"></wiki-ref> on the sensor no wider than 0.03 mm.

after.zh: <wiki-ref to="lens"></wiki-ref>让大光圈进来的光重新会聚，但只对对焦距离上的点准，别处成模糊圈；光圈管亮度，焦距管像的大小。
after.en: A <wiki-ref to="lens"></wiki-ref> brings the light of a wide aperture back together, but only for points at the focus distance; others make blur circles. The aperture sets the light, the focal length the image size.

brief.zh: 调光圈和对焦距离：进光量不低于 4，近处的箱子清晰。
brief.en: Set the aperture and the focus distance: light at least 4, and the near crate sharp.

hint.zh: 光圈开大以后，看两个物体的模糊圈；再看对焦距离改变的是哪一个。
hint.en: After opening the aperture, watch both objects' blur circles; then see which one the focus distance changes.

why.zh: 只把光圈开大：光够了，可箱子不在对焦距离上，它的模糊圈随光圈一起变大。
why.en: Only opening the aperture: the light is enough, but the crate is not at the focus distance and its blur circle grows with the aperture.

why.zh: 只对焦、不开光圈：箱子清晰了，进光量仍然只有 0.16。
why.en: Only focusing, aperture unchanged: the crate is sharp, but the light is still only 0.16.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: <level-ref to="1B4"></level-ref>只要一个物体清晰。这一关有两个标记，近处的在 1200 mm，远处的在 2000 mm；透镜对焦在 1500 mm，不能动。光圈这回用摄影的写法给出：<wiki-ref to="f-number"></wiki-ref>是焦距除以光圈直径，50 mm 镜头的 f/2 就是 25 mm 的光圈。
t.en: <level-ref to="1B4"></level-ref> needed one object sharp. Here there are two markers, the near one at 1200 mm and the far one at 2000 mm; the lens is focused at 1500 mm and stays there. The aperture is now given the photographer's way: the <wiki-ref to="f-number"></wiki-ref> is the focal length over the aperture diameter, so f/2 on a 50 mm lens is a 25 mm aperture.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处两个物体，怎样在一张照片里都清晰？先想好哪一档光圈行，再按「检查」：检查之后，曲线才画出每个深度的模糊圈和清晰的门槛。进光量以 3 mm 光圈的进光为 1。两个标记都清晰、进光量又不低于 1，才算对。
t.en: This level asks: how can a near and a far object both be sharp in one photo? Decide which stop will do before you press Check: only then does the curve draw each depth's blur circle against the sharpness threshold. Light is measured against a 3 mm aperture, which lets in 1. It is right when both markers are sharp and the light is at least 1.

after.zh: 同时清晰的深度范围叫<wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>：光圈越小、f 数越大，它越深，进来的光也越少。
after.en: The range of depths sharp at once is the <wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>: the smaller the aperture, the larger the f-number, the deeper it is and the less light comes in.

brief.zh: 对焦不动，选一档光圈：两个标记都清晰，进光量不低于 1。
brief.en: With the focus fixed, choose an aperture: both markers sharp and the light at least 1.

hint.zh: 检查过 f/2 之后，比较曲线低于门槛的那一段：光圈收小一档，模糊圈和这一段各会怎样？
hint.en: Once f/2 is checked, look at the stretch of the curve below the threshold: one stop smaller, what happens to the blur circles and to that stretch?

hint.zh: 每收小一档，进光量就只剩四分之一。
hint.en: Each stop smaller leaves a quarter of the light.

why.zh: 为了亮把光圈开到最大：清晰范围收窄到对焦处附近，两个标记都落在范围外。
why.en: Opening the aperture fully for light: the sharp range narrows around the focus and both markers fall outside it.

why.zh: 光圈收到最小：两个标记都清晰了，进光量却只剩约 0.27。
why.en: Closing the aperture all the way: both markers are sharp, but the light drops to about 0.27.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth
Sharp front to back, and bright enough

t.zh: <level-ref to="1B5"></level-ref>里对焦不能动，只能靠光圈换景深。这一关新在组合：光圈和对焦距离都能动，两个旋钮互相牵制。两个物体在 1000 mm 和 3000 mm，都要清晰，进光量又不能低于 1。这一关的问题是：既要两个深度都清晰，又要足够的光，对焦该放在哪里？
t.en: In <level-ref to="1B5"></level-ref> the focus was fixed and only the aperture traded depth of field. What is new is the combination: the aperture and the focus distance both turn, and they pull against each other. Two objects stand at 1000 mm and 3000 mm; both must be sharp and the light must not fall below 1. This level asks: with both depths to keep sharp and enough light to gather, where should the focus go?

brief.zh: 同时调光圈和对焦距离：两个物体都清晰，进光量不低于 1。
brief.en: Set the aperture and the focus together: both objects sharp and the light at least 1.

hint.zh: 移动对焦距离时，看曲线低于门槛的那一段跟着往哪里走。
hint.en: As the focus distance moves, watch where the stretch of the curve below the threshold goes.

hint.zh: 清晰范围在对焦距离的两边都有：对焦在一个物体上时，有一边用不上。
hint.en: The sharp range reaches to both sides of the focus: focused on one of the objects, one side goes unused.

why.zh: 对焦在近处，再收光圈直到两个都清晰：进光量只剩 0.25。
why.en: Focusing on the near object and closing down until both are sharp: the light is only 0.25.

why.zh: 光够了，对焦却还在近处：远处的门糊了。
why.en: The light is enough, but the focus is still on the near object: the far door blurs.

why.zh: 对焦挪到远处：近处的人又糊了。
why.en: Moving the focus to the far object: now the near person blurs.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 到这里，像平面一直是无限大的，物体的像总能落上去。真正的相机只有一块传感器：相机台装上一块 20 mm 高、200 像素的传感器，<wiki-ref to="principal-point"></wiki-ref>在中心。像落到传感器边外的物体，不在画面里。
t.en: Until now the image plane has been endless, and every image had somewhere to land. A real camera has only a sensor: the camera bench now holds one 20 mm and 200 pixels tall, its <wiki-ref to="principal-point"></wiki-ref> at the centre. An object whose image falls past its edges is out of the picture.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：要把几个物体全拍进画面，焦距该变长还是变短？三支箭都在 2000 mm 外，台上只有焦距 f 能动。第一个任务要三支都在画面里，中间那支乙又不能太小；第二个任务只拍乙，要它占满画面的高度。
t.en: This level asks: to get several objects into the frame at once, should the focal length grow or shrink? Three arrows stand 2000 mm away, and only the focal length f turns. The first task wants all three in view without the middle arrow B shrinking too far; the second shows B alone and wants it to fill the frame's height.

after.zh: 焦距决定看得多宽，这是<wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>：传感器一定时，焦距短看得宽，焦距长看得窄、物体显得大。
after.en: How wide a camera sees is its <wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>: with the sensor fixed, a short focal length sees wide, a long one narrow, with objects looking larger.

brief.zh: 调焦距，让三支箭的像都落在传感器上，中间那支乙的像又不少于 40 像素高。
brief.en: Set the focal length so all three arrows image on the sensor, with the middle arrow B at least 40 pixels tall.

hint.zh: 看两端那两支箭的像落在哪里，传感器的边又在哪里。
hint.en: See where the two outer arrows image, and where the sensor's edges are.

why.zh: 把焦距拉长想看清楚些：每支箭都变大，两端的落到了传感器外面。
why.en: Lengthening the focal length to see better: every arrow grows, and the outer ones fall off the sensor.

why.zh: 焦距缩到最短：三支都进了画面，乙的像却只剩 20 像素高。
why.en: The focal length as short as it goes: all three are in view, but B's image is only 20 pixels tall.

brief.zh: 只拍中间那支箭：调焦距，让它的像占到画面高度的 95% 以上，又不出画面。
brief.en: Only the middle arrow now: set the focal length so its image fills at least 95% of the frame's height without leaving it.

hint.zh: 上一个任务里读到过视场：焦距变长，它往哪边变？乙要占满 20 mm 的传感器，像要多高？
hint.en: The last task read out the field of view: which way does it move as the focal length grows? To fill the 20 mm sensor, how tall must B's image be?

why.zh: 缩短焦距：视场变宽，这支箭只占画面的一小截。
why.en: Shortening the focal length: the view widens and the arrow covers only a sliver of the frame.

why.zh: 焦距拉得过长：箭的像比传感器还高，上下都出了画面。
why.en: A focal length too long: the arrow's image is taller than the sensor and leaves the frame at both ends.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 相机台上的长度以毫米计，图里的长度以像素计。这台相机的传感器高 20 mm，竖直方向排着 200 个像素。
t.en: Lengths on the camera bench are in millimetres, lengths in the image in pixels. This camera's sensor is 20 mm tall and holds 200 pixels from top to bottom.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：物体在图里高 100 像素，实高 120 mm，离相机 600 mm，镜头的焦距是多少毫米？三个任务：先算出焦距，再到相机台上验证，最后写出以像素计的焦距和这台相机竖直方向的<wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>。
t.en: This level asks: an object is 100 pixels tall in the image, 120 mm tall in reality and 600 mm from the camera — what is the lens's focal length in millimetres? Three tasks: work it out, check it on the camera bench, then give the focal length in pixels and this camera's vertical <wiki-ref to="field-of-view"></wiki-ref>.

after.zh: 物理焦距除以像素尺寸，就是<wiki-ref to="pixel-units"></wiki-ref>：焦距换成图像坐标的单位，视场也能直接用像素算。
after.en: The physical focal length over the pixel size is the <wiki-ref to="pixel-units"></wiki-ref>: the focal length in the image's own units, from which the field of view follows in pixels.

brief.zh: 由像素高、实高和距离，算出镜头的焦距（毫米）。
brief.en: From the height in pixels, the real height and the distance, work out the lens's focal length in millimetres.

hint.zh: 相似三角形两边的长度要用同一种单位。
hint.en: Both sides of the similar triangles must be in one unit.

prompt.zh: 图里高 100 像素，实高 120 mm，距离 600 mm：焦距多少毫米？
prompt.en: 100 pixels tall in the image, 120 mm tall, 600 mm away: how many millimetres is f?

prompt.zh: 图里高 80 像素，实高 400 mm，距离 2000 mm：焦距多少毫米？
prompt.en: 80 pixels tall in the image, 400 mm tall, 2000 mm away: how many millimetres is f?

why.zh: 把像素数当成毫米代进了 h/f = H/Z：100 像素不是 100 mm。传感器 20 mm 排 200 个像素，每个像素 0.1 mm，100 像素只有 10 mm；按 500 mm 的焦距，像会有 100 mm 高，比整块传感器还高。
why.en: That puts the pixel count into h/f = H/Z as millimetres, but 100 pixels are not 100 mm. The sensor holds 200 pixels in 20 mm, so a pixel is 0.1 mm and 100 pixels are 10 mm; at f = 500 mm the image would be 100 mm tall, taller than the whole sensor.

brief.zh: 物高 120 mm、距离 600 mm：调焦距，让像在图里高 100 像素。
brief.en: Object 120 mm tall, 600 mm away: set the focal length so the image is 100 pixels tall.

why.zh: 把 100 像素当成 100 mm 代进比例：像高 100 mm，比整块 20 mm 的传感器还高。
why.en: Putting 100 pixels into the ratio as 100 mm: the image is 100 mm tall, taller than the whole 20 mm sensor.

brief.zh: 这台相机 f = 50 mm，每个像素 0.1 mm：写出它以像素计的焦距和竖直方向的视场。
brief.en: This camera has f = 50 mm and 0.1 mm pixels: give its focal length in pixels and its vertical field of view.

hint.zh: 上一个任务的台子在 f = 50 mm 时读出了以像素计的焦距和视场。
hint.en: At f = 50 mm the bench in the last task read out the focal length in pixels and the field of view.

hint.zh: 从针孔看传感器的上边和下边：半个传感器高除以焦距，是半个视场角的正切。
hint.en: Seen from the pinhole, half the sensor's height over the focal length is the tangent of half the view angle.

prompt.zh: 以像素计的焦距是多少？
prompt.en: What is the focal length in pixels?

prompt.zh: 竖直方向的视场大约多宽？
prompt.en: About how wide is the vertical field of view?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 工作台读得出一个像素的三个数，却没有问过这三个数各是哪种颜色。一张用<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>读进来的照片在这里显示出来，蓝天成了橙色。这一关的问题是：同一张照片，为什么在这里显示出橙色的天空？
t.en: The workbench can read a pixel's three numbers but has never asked which colour each one is. A photo read in with <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref> is displayed here, and its blue sky has turned orange. This level asks: why does the same photo show an orange sky here?

t.zh: 这一关要接一块电路：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。把一个像素的三个数拆开、重排，要用新元件：<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出每个像素第 0、1 或 2 个位置上的数（在元件上设定），组成一张灰度图；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图依次当作 R、G、B，合成一张彩色图。每个像素都和期望相符才算对。
t.en: This level wires a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Taking a pixel's three numbers apart and reordering them needs new parts: <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes the number at position 0, 1 or 2 of every pixel, as set on the part, as a grey image; <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> takes three grey images as R, G and B, in that order, and makes one colour image. It is right when every pixel matches the expected one.

after.zh: 各个库的<wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>不同：<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>读图得到 BGR，<wiki-ref to="matplotlib"></wiki-ref>按 RGB 显示。
after.en: Libraries differ in <wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>: <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref> reads images as BGR, <wiki-ref to="matplotlib"></wiki-ref> displays RGB.

brief.zh: 输入是用 OpenCV 读进来的照片：交出同一张照片，颜色和本来的一样。
brief.en: The input is a photo read with OpenCV: give the same photo in its true colours.

hint.zh: 先把输入原样接到输出，看第一个不同的格子里哪几个数对调了。
hint.en: First wire the input straight to the output, and see which numbers are swapped in the first differing cell.

hint.zh: 把三个位置的数分别取出来看：天空在哪一张里最亮？蓝天本该亮在哪一种颜色上？
hint.en: Take the numbers at the three positions out one by one: in which of them is the sky brightest? Which colour should a blue sky be bright in?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref>弄清了三个数的顺序，还没问它们的大小。电路算出的值可以落在 [0, 1] 之外，比如 −0.2 或 1.2；这样的值画到屏幕上是什么样子，还没有看过。文件里的像素又常存成<wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>：0 到 255 的整数，255 最亮。
t.en: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref> settled the order of the three numbers but not their size. A circuit may compute values outside [0, 1], such as −0.2 or 1.2, and how such values look on a screen has not come up yet. And files often store pixels as <wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>: whole numbers from 0 to 255, 255 the brightest.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：两个像素看上去一样白，存着的数一样吗？第一个任务对照每格存着的数，填出它显示出来的值；第二个任务把 OpenCV 读进来的 uint8 像素写成 [0, 1] 里的 (R, G, B)。每格的数都对才算对。
t.en: This level asks: when two pixels look equally white, do they hold the same number? The first task has you fill in each cell's displayed value from its stored one; the second, write uint8 pixels read by OpenCV as (R, G, B) in [0, 1]. It is right when every cell's numbers are.

after.zh: 像素值有<wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref>和类型：显示时截到两端，存着的数不变；处理时常把 uint8 换成 [0, 1] 的浮点数。
after.en: Pixel values have a <wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref> and a type: the display clips to the ends while the stored numbers stay; processing often turns uint8 into floats in [0, 1].

brief.zh: 对照每格存着的数，填出它在屏幕上显示出来的值。
brief.en: From each cell's stored number, fill in the value the screen displays.

hint.zh: 看画面里最白的几格：它们存的数都一样吗？
hint.en: Look at the whitest cells of the picture: do they all hold the same number?

why.zh: 这是存着的数，不是显示出来的：屏幕只显示得出 0 到 1，−0.2 画成 0，1.2 画成 1，而存着的数照旧不变。
why.en: These are the stored numbers, not the displayed ones: a screen shows only 0 to 1, so −0.2 is drawn as 0 and 1.2 as 1, while the stored numbers stay as they were.

brief.zh: 这两个像素是 OpenCV 读进来的 uint8 值：写成 [0, 1] 里的 (R, G, B)。
brief.en: These two pixels are uint8 values read by OpenCV: write them as (R, G, B) in [0, 1].

hint.zh: OpenCV 读进来的三个数按什么顺序排？
hint.en: In what order does OpenCV store the three numbers?

why.zh: 除以 255 没错，顺序却照 RGB 读了：OpenCV 读进来的三个数是 B、G、R，第一个数是蓝。
why.en: Dividing by 255 is right, but the numbers were read as RGB: OpenCV stores B, G, R, so the first number is blue.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 工作台能读写每个像素，却只能照原样摆放：一张图要放大或缩小，它没有办法。缩放和取出一部分不同，要给新图的每个像素算出一个值；算值之前，先得知道这个像素落在原图的什么位置。
t.en: The workbench can read and write every pixel, but only where it already is: it cannot enlarge or shrink an image. Unlike taking out a part, resizing computes a value for every pixel of the new image; before any value, it must know where that pixel sits in the original.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：图像放大或缩小时，新图的每个像素对应原图的什么位置？约定是新旧两排像素一样长、像素中心对齐。第一个任务在格子上手算一行，第二个任务搭一块电路，交出整张新图的两张源坐标图，测试的坐标都对才算对。
t.en: This level asks: when an image is enlarged or shrunk, where in the original does each new pixel sit? The convention: the old and the new row are equally long and pixel centres are aligned. The first task works out one row by hand on the grid; the second wires a circuit that gives the whole new image's two source-coordinate images, right when every tested coordinate is.

desc.zh: 输入原图的宽 sw、高 sh 和新图的宽 nw、高 nh，输出新图每个像素在原图里的 x、y（两张坐标图）
desc.en: Takes the original's width sw and height sh and the new width nw and height nh; gives each new pixel's x and y in the original (two coordinate images)

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>：每个新像素反向映射回原图，不把旧像素正向搬过去；各个库的对齐约定不同，要写明。
after.en: This is a <wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>: each new pixel mapped back into the original, not old pixels pushed forwards; libraries align differently, so the convention must be stated.

brief.zh: 这一行 2 像素宽，放大成 3 像素：写出每个新像素在原图里的 x。
brief.en: This row, 2 pixels wide, is enlarged to 3: write where each new pixel sits in the original, as x.

hint.zh: 把新旧两排画成等长的两条，各自的像素中心落在哪里？
hint.en: Draw the two rows as two bars of one length: where does each pixel centre fall?

after.zh: 新像素不是旧像素换了编号：中间那个落在两个旧像素之间。
after.en: New pixels are not old ones renumbered: the middle one falls between two old pixels.

label.zh: 新像素在原图里的 x

why.zh: 这是把新像素当成旧像素重新编号：原图这一行只有 x = 0 和 x = 1 两个像素，x = 2 落在原图外面。新旧两排一样长，三个新像素中心要分布在两个旧像素占的那段长度上。
why.en: That renumbers the new pixels as if they were old ones: the original row has pixels at x = 0 and x = 1 only, so x = 2 lies outside it. The two rows are equally long, so the three new centres spread over the length the two old pixels cover.

t.zh: 手算一行可以，一整张图要每个像素各算一遍，就要电路了：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。新图的每个像素先要有自己的坐标，而手上没有元件能从两个数造出一整张图。
t.en: One row works by hand; a whole image, every pixel worked out, needs a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Each new pixel first needs its own coordinates, and no part in hand makes a whole image out of two numbers.

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref>给定宽和高，给出每格就是自己 x、y 的两张坐标图。坐标还要换算：<part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref>给出一个固定的数，<part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref>对数和整张图逐个值地算。
t.en: The new part <part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref> takes a width and a height and gives the two coordinate images whose cells hold their own x and y. The coordinates still need converting: <part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref> gives a fixed number, and <part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>, <part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref> and <part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref> work value by value on numbers and whole images.

brief.zh: 输入原图和新图的宽高：交出新图每个像素在原图里的 x 坐标图和 y 坐标图。
brief.en: Given the original's and the new width and height, give the image of each new pixel's x in the original, and the image of its y.

hint.zh: 先给新图的每个像素一对它自己的坐标。
hint.en: First give every pixel of the new image its own pair of coordinates.

hint.zh: 新图的一个像素宽，相当于原图的几个像素宽？像素中心和像素左边差多少？
hint.en: One pixel of the new image is how many pixels of the original wide? How far is a pixel's centre from its left edge?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 识别网络要 S×S 的输入，照片却有各种宽高。手上的缩放元件能把任何图缩成任何尺寸。这一关的问题是：网络要 512×512，手里是 768×512 的照片，直接缩放到 512×512 可以吗？
t.en: A recognition network wants S×S input, while photos come in every width and height. The resizers in hand can bring any image to any size. This level asks: the network wants 512×512 and the photo is 768×512 — can it be resized straight to 512×512?

t.zh: 测试图里画着一个正方形的东西：交出的 S×S 图里，它还得是正方形。结果里每个像素都来自照片，不留空边；它的中心对准照片的中心，对不准时偏左上半个像素。横幅和竖幅的照片都要成立。
t.en: The test images hold something square, and in the S×S result it must still be square. Every pixel of the result comes from the photo, with no empty borders, and it is centred on the photo's centre, half a pixel towards the top-left where it cannot be exact. It must work for landscape and portrait photos alike.

after.zh: 宽与高之比叫<wiki-ref to="aspect-ratio"></wiki-ref>：宽高各缩各的会改变它，圆变成椭圆；OpenCV 的尺寸写成 (宽, 高)。
after.en: Width over height is the <wiki-ref to="aspect-ratio"></wiki-ref>: scaling width and height separately changes it and turns circles into ellipses; OpenCV writes a size as (width, height).

brief.zh: 输入一张照片和边长 S：交出 S×S 的图，照片里的正方形在图里仍是正方形，画面居中。
brief.en: Given a photo and a side S, give an S×S image, centred on the photo, in which squares stay square.

hint.zh: 宽和高乘同一个数，宽高比才不变。
hint.en: Only multiplying width and height by one number keeps their ratio.

hint.zh: 缩放和裁剪都要整数的宽高。
hint.en: Resizing and cropping both need whole-number sizes.

solution: c = crop(r, x0, y0, S, S)

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 有了<part-ref to="sampleGrid"></part-ref>，每个新像素都知道自己落在原图的哪里；可这个位置一般不是整数，原图在那里没有像素。手上的元件只在同一个位置上算，没有一个能把原图某处的值搬到新图上。
t.en: With the <part-ref to="sampleGrid"></part-ref> every new pixel knows where it sits in the original; but that position is seldom a whole number, and the original has no pixel there. The parts in hand compute in place, and none can carry a value from somewhere in the original to the new image.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：放大一张图时，落在两个旧像素之间的新像素，值从哪里来？新元件<part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref>按整数坐标在图上取值，<part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref>读出图的宽高，<part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref>把连续的数变成整数。离两边一样远时，约定取坐标较大的一边。输出图逐格和期望相符才算对。
t.en: This level asks: when an image is enlarged, where does a new pixel that falls between two old ones get its value? New parts: <part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref> reads an image at whole-number coordinates, <part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref> gives an image's width and height, and <part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref> turns a continuous number into a whole one. When a position is equally far from two pixels, the convention takes the larger coordinate. It is right when the output matches the expected image cell by cell.

desc.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽 w、高 h，输出缩放后的图：每个新像素取原图里离它最近的像素
desc.en: Takes an image and a new width w and height h; gives the resized image, each new pixel the original pixel nearest to it

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>：快、边缘硬，放大后成块；OpenCV 里叫 INTER_NEAREST。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>: fast, with hard edges, and blocky when enlarged; OpenCV calls it INTER_NEAREST.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽、高：交出缩放后的图，每个新像素照抄原图里离它最近的那个像素。
brief.en: Given an image and a new width and height, give the resized image, each new pixel copying the original pixel nearest to it.

hint.zh: 取像素只接受整数坐标，也不接受原图外面的坐标。
hint.en: The lookup takes only whole-number coordinates, and none outside the image.

hint.zh: 离一个坐标最近的整数，和它向下取整得到的整数，什么时候不一样？
hint.en: When does the whole number nearest a coordinate differ from the one rounding down gives?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: <level-ref to="1D2"></level-ref>里放大成块，但每个旧像素都还在。这一关换一个方向：最近邻缩小图像时，没被选中的旧像素去了哪里？第一个任务把条纹图缩到一半宽、再放大回原宽，同时交出每个新像素的采样位置；第二个任务判断原图的哪些列留在了结果里。
t.en: In <level-ref to="1D2"></level-ref> enlarging came out blocky, but every old pixel was still there. This level goes the other way: when nearest neighbour shrinks an image, what becomes of the old pixels it does not pick? The first task shrinks striped images to half their width and back again, giving each new pixel's sample position too; the second judges which of the original's columns survive.

brief.zh: 把输入的图缩到一半宽（高不变），交出缩小的图、每个新像素在原图里的 x，以及缩小的图再放大回原宽的样子。
brief.en: Shrink the input to half its width (height unchanged), and give the shrunk image, each new pixel's x in the original, and the shrunk image enlarged back to the original width.

hint.zh: 缩小后再放大，宽回来了：原图里的值也都回来了吗？
hint.en: Shrinking and then enlarging brings the width back: does it bring back every value of the original too?

brief.zh: 选出值留在了缩小结果里的那些原图列。
brief.en: Choose the original columns whose values survive in the shrunk result.

hint.zh: 每个新像素只读原图的一列。
hint.en: Each new pixel reads one column of the original.

prompt.zh: 这一行 8 像素宽，最近邻缩到 4 像素：哪几列的值留了下来？
prompt.en: This row, 8 pixels wide, is shrunk to 4 by nearest neighbour: which columns' values survive?

prompt.zh: 这一行 9 像素宽，最近邻缩到 3 像素：哪几列的值留了下来？
prompt.en: This row, 9 pixels wide, is shrunk to 3 by nearest neighbour: which columns' values survive?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref>只会照抄：新像素的值只能是原图里已有的某一个，[0, 1] 放大成 3 像素，中间那个不是 0 就是 1。这一关的问题是：新像素落在两个旧像素之间时，它只能等于其中一个吗？
t.en: The <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref> only copies: a new pixel can take only a value the original already has, so [0, 1] enlarged to 3 pixels has a middle of either 0 or 1. This level asks: when a new pixel falls between two old ones, must it equal one of them?

t.zh: 测试要的是：[0, 1] 放大成 3 像素时，中间那个是 0.5。这一关的图都只有一行。搭出的元件输入一张图和新的宽、高，交出缩放后的图，测试和隐藏测试的每个值都对才算对。
t.en: The tests want [0, 1] enlarged to 3 pixels to have 0.5 in the middle. This level's images are all one row high. The part takes an image and a new width and height and gives the resized image, right when every value in the tests and hidden tests is.

desc.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽 w、高 h，输出缩放后的图：每个新像素由左右两个旧像素按距离加权
desc.en: Takes an image and a new width w and height h; gives the resized image, each new pixel weighted from the old pixels to its left and right by distance

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：两边按距离加权，权重之和为 1，新值介于两边之间。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: the two sides weighted by distance, the weights summing to 1, the new value lying between them.

brief.zh: 输入一行像素和新的宽、高：交出缩放后的图，每个新像素的值取自它左右两个旧像素。
brief.en: Given a row of pixels and a new width and height, give the resized image, each new pixel's value taken from the two old pixels on its left and right.

hint.zh: 中间那个新像素离左右两个旧像素各有多远？
hint.en: How far is the middle new pixel from each of the two old ones?

hint.zh: 先找出新位置左边那个旧像素，再算新位置离它有多远。
hint.en: First find the old pixel to the left of the new position, then how far the position is from it.

hint.zh: 两端的新位置落在原图之外：取像素可以设成取最近的边。
hint.en: The new positions at the ends fall outside the original: the lookup can be set to read the nearest edge.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>只沿一行插值，竖直方向照抄离得最近的那一行。放大一张二维的图，新像素在上下方向也落在两行之间。这一关的问题是：在二维图像里，落在四个旧像素中间的新像素，值怎么算？
t.en: The <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref> interpolates only along a row and copies the nearest row vertically. Enlarging a 2D image, a new pixel also falls between two rows. This level asks: in a 2D image, how is the value of a new pixel among four old ones computed?

t.zh: 两个任务：先用手上的线性缩放只改一张图的宽度，看它在每一行上做了什么；再升级这个元件，让新像素的值由周围四个旧像素决定。升级后的元件要通过二维放大和缩小的测试。
t.en: Two tasks: first use the linear resizer in hand to change only an image's width and see what it does on each row; then upgrade the part so a new pixel's value comes from the four old pixels around it. The upgraded part must pass tests that enlarge and shrink in two dimensions.

desc.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽 w、高 h，输出缩放后的图：每个新像素由周围四个旧像素按距离加权（双线性）
desc.en: Takes an image and a new width w and height h; gives the resized image, each new pixel weighted from the four old pixels around it by distance (bilinear)

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：新值是四个邻居的加权平均，比最近邻平滑；OpenCV 里叫 INTER_LINEAR。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: the new value a weighted average of four neighbours, smoother than nearest neighbour; OpenCV calls it INTER_LINEAR.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽：交出只改了宽度、高度不变的图。
brief.en: Given an image and a new width, give the image with only its width changed, its height as it was.

after.zh: 每一行各自沿 x 插值，行和行之间没有混合。
after.en: Each row is interpolated along x on its own; rows are never mixed.

brief.zh: 升级线性缩放：输入一张图和新的宽、高，新像素由周围四个旧像素按距离加权。
brief.en: Upgrade the linear resize: given an image and a new width and height, each new pixel weighted from the four old pixels around it by distance.

hint.zh: 竖直方向也有一个距离：新位置离上面那一行有多远。
hint.en: There is a vertical distance too: how far the new position is from the row above.

hint.zh: 上下两行各沿 x 插一次，得到两个值，再在它们之间沿 y 插一次。
hint.en: Interpolate along x on the row above and on the row below, then along y between the two results.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 手上有两种缩放：<part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref>和<part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>。这一关新在取舍：用它们放大同一张图，结果差在哪里？是不是总有一种更好？三个任务：先并排放大，再把结果认到剖面上，最后找出推翻「双线性总比最近邻好」的那组结果。
t.en: Two resizers are in hand: the <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref> and the <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>. What is new is the trade-off: enlarging one image with each, how do the results differ, and is one always better? Three tasks: enlarge side by side, match the results to profiles, then find the result that refutes 'bilinear is always better than nearest neighbour'.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽、高：交出最近邻和双线性各自缩放的结果。
brief.en: Given an image and a new width and height, give the nearest-neighbour and the bilinear results.

brief.zh: 为两种放大的结果各选出它的剖面。
brief.en: For each of the two enlargements, choose its profile.

prompt.zh: [0, 1] 用最近邻放大到 5 像素
prompt.en: [0, 1] enlarged to 5 pixels by nearest neighbour

prompt.zh: [0, 1] 用双线性放大到 5 像素
prompt.en: [0, 1] enlarged to 5 pixels by bilinear

prompt.zh: [0, 0, 1, 1] 用双线性放大到 8 像素
prompt.en: [0, 0, 1, 1] enlarged to 8 pixels by bilinear

prompt.zh: [0, 0, 1, 1] 用最近邻放大到 8 像素
prompt.en: [0, 0, 1, 1] enlarged to 8 pixels by nearest neighbour

brief.zh: 选出说明「双线性总比最近邻好」不成立的那组结果。
brief.en: Choose the result that shows 'bilinear is always better than nearest neighbour' does not hold.

hint.zh: 有的图里，每个值都有固定的含义，两者之间的值没有意义。
hint.en: In some images every value has a fixed meaning, and values in between mean nothing.

prompt.zh: 哪一组结果是反例？
prompt.en: Which result is a counterexample?

label.en: a segmentation label map (0 background, 1 object) [0, 1], bilinear: [0, 0.25, 0.75, 1]

prompt.zh: 这一批里，哪一组结果是反例？
prompt.en: In this batch, which result is a counterexample?

label.en: a class id map (1 road, 3 pedestrian) [1, 3], bilinear: [1, 1.5, 2.5, 3]

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 电路算出的值是任意的实数，还可能越出 [0, 1]；图像存进文件时，每个值却只能取有限的几级，比如 0 到 255 的整数，共 256 级。工作台还没有办法把一个值存成其中一级。
t.en: The values a circuit computes are arbitrary real numbers and may leave [0, 1]; stored in a file, though, each value can take only finitely many levels, whole numbers from 0 to 255, say, 256 in all. The workbench has no way yet to store a value as one of them.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：一个值只能存成 L 级中的一级时，该存哪一级？L 级把 [0, 1] 等分，L = 3 时是 0、0.5、1；正好在两级中间时，约定取较大的一级。越出 [0, 1] 的值要先截回来，而加减乘除和向下取整都定不出上下界：新元件<part-ref to="part:min"></part-ref>和<part-ref to="part:max"></part-ref>逐个值取两者中小的、大的。
t.en: This level asks: when a value can only be stored as one of L levels, which should it be? L levels divide [0, 1] evenly: with L = 3 they are 0, 0.5 and 1; a value exactly between two levels goes to the larger, by convention. Values outside [0, 1] must be brought back first, and neither arithmetic nor floor can set a bound: the new parts <part-ref to="part:min"></part-ref> and <part-ref to="part:max"></part-ref> take the smaller and the larger of two, value by value.

desc.zh: 输入一张图和级数 L，输出量化后的图：先截到 [0, 1]，再存成最近的一级
desc.en: Takes an image and a number of levels L; gives the quantised image: clipped to [0, 1], then stored as the nearest level

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="quantisation"></wiki-ref>：把连续的值存成有限的几级，取最近的一级，不是截掉小数；uint8 就是 256 级。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="quantisation"></wiki-ref>: storing continuous values as finitely many levels, the nearest one, not the fraction cut off; uint8 has 256 levels.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和级数 L：截到 [0, 1] 以后，每个值存成离它最近的一级。
brief.en: Given an image and a number of levels L, clip to [0, 1], then store each value as the level nearest to it.

hint.zh: 乘上 L − 1 以后，每一级正好落在一个整数上。
hint.en: Multiplied by L − 1, every level lands on a whole number.

hint.zh: −0.2 和 1.3 这样的值会算出不存在的级。
hint.en: Values such as −0.2 and 1.3 give levels that do not exist.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: <part-ref to="quantise"></part-ref>把每个值存成最近的一级。这一关新在辨真伪：量化以后，原来的值还能找回来吗？第一个任务让量化器存一张图，同时交出每一格的原值可能落在的范围；第二个任务反过来，从几组输入里选出存成同一个结果的全部输入。
t.en: The <part-ref to="quantise"></part-ref> stores each value as the nearest level. What is new is testing a belief: after quantisation, can the original values be recovered? The first task has the quantiser store an image and give, for each cell, the range its original may lie in; the second goes backwards and picks, among several inputs, every one stored as the same result.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和级数 L：交出量化的结果，以及每一格的原值可能在的范围，从 low 到 high（都在 [0, 1] 里）。
brief.en: Given an image and a number of levels L, give the quantised result and, for each cell, the range its original may lie in, from low to high (both within [0, 1]).

hint.zh: 相邻两级隔多远？一个值离它存成的那一级，最远能有多远？
hint.en: How far apart are two neighbouring levels? How far can a value lie from the level it is stored as?

brief.zh: 选出量化以后和给出的结果完全相同的全部输入。
brief.en: Choose every input whose quantised result is exactly the one given.

hint.zh: 把每组输入逐个值算一遍，看它存成哪一级。
hint.en: Work each input through value by value, and see which level it is stored as.

prompt.zh: 存成 3 级以后得到 [0, 0.5] 的输入有哪些？
prompt.en: Which inputs become [0, 0.5] when stored in 3 levels?

prompt.zh: 存成 2 级以后得到 [0, 1] 的输入有哪些？
prompt.en: Which inputs become [0, 1] when stored in 2 levels?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 流水线常常只要图里的一部分，比如物体所在的那一片。手上的<part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref>改的是整张图的尺寸，每个输出像素都在整张图上采样。这一关的问题是：从一张图里取出一部分时，输出的像素值是原图里已有的，还是新算出来的？
t.en: A pipeline often wants only part of an image, the region where an object is, say. The <part-ref to="resizeNearest"></part-ref> in hand changes the whole image's size, every output pixel sampled across the whole image. This level asks: when part of an image is taken out, are the output's pixel values ones the original holds, or newly computed?

t.zh: 输入一张图、窗口左上角的 x0、y0 和窗口的宽 w、高 h。交出窗口里的像素，测试逐格和原图核对；隐藏测试里有贴边的窗口和彩色图。
t.en: The inputs are an image, the window's top-left x0, y0, and its width w and height h. Give the pixels inside the window; the tests check them cell by cell against the original, and hidden tests include windows on the border and a colour image.

desc.zh: 输入一张图、窗口左上角 x0、y0 和宽 w、高 h，输出窗口里的像素，值原样不变
desc.en: Takes an image, a window's top-left x0, y0 and its width w and height h; gives the pixels inside the window, values unchanged

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>：取原数组的子区域，像素值原样保留。<wiki-ref to="numpy"></wiki-ref>写成 image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w]。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>: a sub-region of the original array, its pixel values kept as they are. In <wiki-ref to="numpy"></wiki-ref> it is image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w].

brief.zh: 输入一张图、窗口左上角 (x0, y0) 和宽 w、高 h：交出窗口里的像素。
brief.en: Given an image, a window's top-left corner (x0, y0) and its width w and height h, give the pixels inside the window.

hint.zh: 窗口里坐标 (x, y) 的像素，是原图里的哪一个？
hint.en: Which pixel of the original is the window's pixel at (x, y)?

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

t.zh: 手上已经有<part-ref to="crop"></part-ref>和<part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref>。手机的数码变焦没有换镜头，它只有已经拍下的像素。这一关的问题是：它怎样把画面中间放大 k 倍？交出的图和输入一样大，显示原图中心那一部分放大 k 倍后的样子；隐藏测试有非正方形的图和别的 k。
t.en: The <part-ref to="crop"></part-ref> and the <part-ref to="resizeLinear"></part-ref> are in hand. A phone's digital zoom changes no lens; all it has are the pixels already taken. This level asks: how does it magnify the middle of the picture k times? The result is as large as the input and shows the part at the original's centre magnified k times; hidden tests use non-square images and other k.

after.zh: 数码变焦等于先<wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref>、再放大：它只用已有的像素，不带来新的细节；光学变焦换的是镜头的焦距。
after.en: Digital zoom is <wiki-ref to="cropping"></wiki-ref> followed by enlarging: it uses only the pixels already there and adds no detail; optical zoom changes the lens's focal length.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和倍数 k：交出同样大小的图，内容是原图中心那个宽、高各为 1/k 的窗口放大 k 倍，只用窗口里的像素。
brief.en: Given an image and a factor k, give an image of the same size showing the window at the original's centre, 1/k as wide and as tall, magnified k times, made from the pixels inside that window only.

hint.zh: 变焦后的画面只用得到原图的哪些像素？先把它们取出来。
hint.en: Which pixels of the original can the zoomed picture use? Take those out first.

hint.zh: 窗口宽是原宽的 1/k，左右两边各留下多少？
hint.en: The window is 1/k of the width: how much is left over on each side?

solution: c = crop(image, x0, y0, cw, ch)
naive: c = crop(big, zero, zero, s.w, s.h)

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

value.zh: 先弄清一张图能回答什么，再从一格格的数起步，搭出相机模型和读图、缩放、量化、裁剪的电路：场景怎样变成一组数，这组数又怎样被处理。
value.en: First learn what one image can answer; then, starting from cells of numbers, build camera models and circuits that read, resize, quantise and crop images: how a scene becomes an array of numbers, and how that array is handled.

question.zh: 一个视觉系统能被问什么，一张图又能回答什么？
question.en: What can a vision system be asked, and what can one image answer?

question.zh: 场景怎样变成一组数，这组数又怎样被裁剪、缩放和存下来？
question.en: How does a scene become an array of numbers, and how is that array cropped, resized and stored?

body.zh: Python 的数组库。图像在里面是一个数组，形状写成 (高, 宽, 通道)，下标先行后列：image[y, x]。切片 image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w] 取出一块；切片返回的常是原数组的视图，要单独修改时先 .copy()。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲与 workshop 2。
body.en: Python's array library. An image is an array whose shape is written (height, width, channels), indexed row first: image[y, x]. The slice image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w] takes out a region; a slice is often a view of the original array, so copy it with .copy() before changing it on its own. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 and workshop 2.

body.zh: 无符号 8 位整数，像素最常见的存法：每个值是 0 到 255 的整数，黑是 0，白是 255，RGB 里的纯红是 [255, 0, 0]。相加、相乘容易溢出，所以处理时常换成 float32 并缩到 [0, 1]，算完再明确地换回去。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，数据类型（幻灯片 26）与 workshop 2。
body.en: The unsigned 8-bit integer, the commonest way to store pixels: each value a whole number from 0 to 255, black 0, white 255, pure red in RGB [255, 0, 0]. Sums and products overflow easily, so processing often converts to float32 scaled to [0, 1] and casts back explicitly at the end. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, data types (slide 26), and workshop 2.

body.zh: Python 的绘图库。matplotlib.pyplot.imshow 按 RGB 显示彩色图，所以 OpenCV 读进来的 BGR 图要先用 cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB) 换通道顺序再显示；这一步只换顺序，不改内容和尺寸。出处：COMP90086 workshop 2。
body.en: Python's plotting library. matplotlib.pyplot.imshow displays colour images as RGB, so a BGR image read by OpenCV is first converted with cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB); this changes only the channel order, not the content or the size. Source: COMP90086 workshop 2.

body.zh: 光轴穿过像平面的那一点，像平面上量位置的起点。理想相机的主点在传感器正中，视场两边对称；真实相机的主点会有偏移，要和像素尺寸、镜头畸变一起考虑。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与焦距（幻灯片 11、15）。
body.en: The point where the optical axis meets the image plane, from which positions on the plane are measured. In an ideal camera it sits at the centre of the sensor and the field of view is symmetric; in a real camera it is offset and must be accounted for along with the pixel size and lens distortion. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and focal length (slides 11, 15).

body.zh: 摄影上写光圈的方式：f 数 = 焦距 / 光圈直径，写成 f/2、f/5.6、f/32。同一支镜头，f 数越大，光圈越小。70 mm 镜头在 f/5.6 时，光圈直径约为 70/5.6 = 12.5 mm。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，光圈与景深（幻灯片 16）。
body.en: Photography's way of writing the aperture: f-number = focal length / aperture diameter, written f/2, f/5.6, f/32. On one lens, the larger the f-number, the smaller the aperture. A 70 mm lens at f/5.6 has an aperture about 70/5.6 = 12.5 mm across. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, aperture and depth of field (slide 16).

body.zh: 一点射出的光经过透镜，在传感器上落成的那个小圆，也叫弥散圆。点在对焦距离上时，它缩成一点；不在时，它有一定大小，这一点就显得糊。模糊圈小于一个门槛（比如一个像素的大小）时，就算清晰。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，相机为什么需要透镜（幻灯片 12–13）。
body.en: The small disc that the light from one point makes on the sensor after the lens, also called the circle of confusion. For a point at the focus distance it shrinks to a point; otherwise it has some size and the point looks blurred. A blur circle below a threshold, such as one pixel's size, counts as sharp. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, why cameras need lenses (slides 12–13).

body.zh: 镜头放光进来的开口，大小用直径 D 表示（台上记作 A）。它管进来多少光；管像的大小的是焦距。光圈小，接近针孔，进光少；光圈大，进光多。摄影上用 f 数写光圈。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，透镜与光圈（幻灯片 13、16）。
body.en: The opening through which a lens lets light in, its size given as the diameter D (A on the bench). It sets how much light comes in; the image size is the focal length's business. A small aperture comes close to a pinhole and lets in little light; a large one lets in more. Photography writes the aperture as an f-number. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, lens and aperture (slides 13, 16).

body.zh: 针孔相机里是针孔到像平面的距离 f，透镜相机里是镜头的焦距。它管像的大小，和管进光量的光圈直径是两个不同的长度，不能混为一谈。像平面上它以毫米计，在数字图像里常换成以像素计。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与透镜（幻灯片 11、13）。
body.en: In a pinhole camera, the distance f from the hole to the image plane; in a lens camera, the lens's focal length. It sets the image size and is a different length from the aperture diameter, which sets the light; the two are not to be confused. On the image plane it is in millimetres; for digital images it is often converted to pixels. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and lenses (slides 11, 13).

body.zh: 针孔相机里光线穿过针孔后落上的平面，讲义也叫成像平面；它离针孔的距离是焦距 f。真实相机的传感器在针孔后面，像是倒的；讲义把像平面画在针孔前面，像不倒过来，也省掉负号。这是坐标约定，不是传感器真正的位置。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与成像模型（幻灯片 11、18）。
body.en: The plane that rays reach after passing a pinhole camera's hole, at the focal length f from it. In a real camera the sensor is behind the hole and the image is upside down; the lectures draw the image plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright and the minus signs go away. This is a coordinate convention, not where the sensor really is. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and the image formation model (slides 11, 18).

body.zh: 常用的开源计算机视觉库，Python 里写作 cv2。用它时要记住它自己的约定：尺寸写成 (宽, 高)，和 NumPy 数组的形状 (高, 宽, 通道) 相反；cv2.imread 读进来的彩色图按 BGR 排通道；缩放的插值方式有 INTER_NEAREST、INTER_LINEAR 等。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲与 workshop 2。
body.en: A widely used open-source computer vision library, cv2 in Python. Its own conventions must be kept in mind: a size is written (width, height), the reverse of a NumPy array's shape (height, width, channels); cv2.imread reads colour images with their channels in BGR order; its resizing interpolations include INTER_NEAREST and INTER_LINEAR. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 and workshop 2.

body.zh: 彩色图比灰度图多出的那一维：每个像素按通道存几个数，最常见的是红、绿、蓝三个。三个通道是相机和人眼视觉的工程表示（人眼有三类主要的视锥细胞），不是说自然界只有三种颜色。取出一个通道，得到的是一张灰度图。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，图像张量（幻灯片 22）。
body.en: The axis a colour image has beyond a greyscale one: each pixel stores one number per channel, most often three, for red, green and blue. Three channels are an engineering representation shared by cameras and human vision (the eye has three main kinds of cone), not a claim that nature has only three colours. One channel taken out is a greyscale image. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the image tensor (slide 22).

body.zh: 数字图像的一格。灰度图里一个像素是一个数，说那里有多亮；彩色图里是几个数，每个通道一个。像素只记下亮度和颜色，不记下这一点离相机多远。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，成像与图像张量（幻灯片 8、22）。
body.en: One cell of a digital image. In a greyscale image a pixel is one number, how bright that place is; in a colour image it is several numbers, one per channel. A pixel records brightness and colour, not how far that point is from the camera. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, image formation and the image tensor (slides 8, 22).

body.zh: 一个物体挡在另一个前面，被挡住的部分在图像里没有一个像素。它是识别难的原因之一：同一个物体露出的部分不同，看上去就不同。被整个挡住的东西，图像既不能证实，也不能否定，连「它不在场景里」也说不出。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，识别为什么难（幻灯片 28）。
body.en: One object stands in front of another, and the hidden part has no pixel at all in the image. It is one reason recognition is hard: one object looks different depending on what part of it shows. Of something entirely hidden the image can confirm nothing and deny nothing — not even that it is absent from the scene. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, why recognition is hard (slide 28).

body.zh: 已知物体、材质、灯光和相机，向前生成一张图像：这是正问题。计算机视觉走反方向，从图像推测这些东西。实际系统常把两者放在一起：按当前的估计渲染一张预测图，和真实的图比较，再用差异修正估计，叫 render and compare。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉与图形学（幻灯片 8）。
body.en: Given objects, materials, lights and a camera, generate an image forwards: a forward problem. Computer vision goes the other way, inferring these from the image. Real systems often combine the two: render a predicted image from the current estimate, compare it with the real one and correct the estimate by the difference — render and compare. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision and graphics (slide 8).

body.zh: 刻意扰动过的输入：只改动很少的像素，人眼几乎看不出变化，却能让神经网络把一个数字判成另一个数字，或把 dog 判成 hot dog，而且置信度很高。它说明模型在常见的照片上答得好，不等于它对输入的变化鲁棒。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，对抗样本（幻灯片 2–3）。
body.en: An input perturbed on purpose: a few altered pixels, a change the eye hardly sees, make a neural network read one digit as another or a dog as a hot dog, and with high confidence. It shows that answering ordinary photos well does not make a model robust to changes in its input. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, adversarial examples (slides 2–3).

body.zh: 和图像一样大的一张图，每格是那一点离相机的距离，例如以米计。它是三维恢复的一种输出，回答「多远」。它的数是长度，可以比较远近、相减；类别图和实例图里的数是编号，不能当距离用。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（三维恢复，幻灯片 7）。
body.en: A map as large as the image whose every cell holds that point's distance from the camera, in metres say. It is one output of 3D reconstruction and answers 'how far'. Its numbers are lengths, which can be compared and subtracted; the numbers in a class map or an instance map are ids and cannot serve as distances. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (3D reconstruction, slide 7).

body.zh: 给每个像素标出它属于哪一类（道路、天空、人）。它只说「哪一类」，不说「哪一个」：同一类的几个物体挨在一起时连成一片，从图上数不出个数。要分开同类的各个物体，用实例分割。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: Labels each pixel with the class it belongs to (road, sky, person).
